title: If you have multiple interests, do not waste the next 2-3 years

sentences.en: If you have multiple interests and you don't know how to manage them, or you don't know what options there are for you in the future, then I have good news for you because this is the greatest time to be alive.
sentences.zh: 如果你有多重兴趣，却不知道怎么管理它们，或者不知道未来有什么选择等着你，那我有个好消息——因为这是有史以来最好的时代。

sentences.en: But in lies the problem.
sentences.zh: 但问题恰恰就在这里。

sentences.en: Society has made you feel like having multiple interests is a weakness.
sentences.zh: 社会让你觉得，有多重兴趣是一种弱点。

sentences.en: We all know the story, right?
sentences.zh: 这个故事我们都熟，对吧？

sentences.en: You go to school, you get a job.
sentences.zh: 上学，找工作。

sentences.en: You retire at some point.
sentences.zh: 然后在某个节点退休。

sentences.en: But there is so much wrong with that series of events.
sentences.zh: 但这套流程的问题太大了。

sentences.en: I feel like a lot of people fail to understand that we don't live in the industrial age anymore, but we are still dealing with its consequences.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多人没意识到，我们已经不在工业时代了，却还在承受它的后果。

sentences.en: Specializing in only one skill is certain death.
sentences.zh: 只专精一项技能，等于死路一条。

sentences.en: And I feel like we all know by now how dangerous mechanical living is for the psyche and soul.
sentences.zh: 而且我想大家现在都明白，机械式生活对心灵和灵魂有多危险。

sentences.en: It's not meaningful, right?
sentences.zh: 它没有意义，对吧？

sentences.en: We've made productivity our God and that God has betrayed us.
sentences.zh: 我们把生产力当成了神，而这个神背叛了我们。

sentences.en: And I also think that people feel that we are going through a second renaissance.
sentences.zh: 我还觉得，人们能感受到我们正在经历第二次文艺复兴。

sentences.en: So you're very excited, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你特别兴奋，对吧？

sentences.en: You have multiple interests.
sentences.zh: 你有多重兴趣。

sentences.en: You're like, oh, okay, how do I actually make the most of this?
sentences.zh: 你会想，好，那我怎么才能真正用好这些兴趣？

sentences.en: I see people online and they're doing these cool things.
sentences.zh: 我在网上看到别人在做很酷的事。

sentences.en: I get to listen to people who talk about my interests, but how do I do something similar?
sentences.zh: 我能听到有人聊我感兴趣的话题，但我怎么才能做出类似的东西？

sentences.en: You have to understand that your curiosity and love for learning is not a weakness.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，你的好奇心和对学习的热爱不是弱点。

sentences.en: It is a massive advantage.
sentences.zh: 它是一个巨大的优势。

sentences.en: You just need to learn what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 你只需要学会怎么用它。

sentences.en: And I felt the same way for the longest time.
sentences.zh: 我有很长一段时间也是这种感觉。

sentences.en: I would just learn and learn and learn and watch tutorials get stuck in tutorial hell.
sentences.zh: 我就是不停地学、学、学，看教程，陷在教程地狱里出不来。

sentences.en: I would see people online say to avoid shiny object syndrome and I'd be like, damn, I'm right in the middle of that. I need to change what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 看到网上有人说要避免"闪亮物体综合征"，我就想，完了，我正深陷其中，我得改变做法。

sentences.en: I need to focus on one thing, and I got my dopamine from feeling smart.
sentences.zh: 我得专注在一件事上，而我的多巴胺来自"觉得自己很聪明"。

sentences.en: But when I looked back at my life, I didn't really have anything to show for it.
sentences.zh: 但当我回头看自己的人生，我其实拿不出任何成果。

sentences.en: I felt smart, I couldn't articulate anything that I remembered, but my life didn't change all that much.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己聪明，却说不出任何真正记住的东西，而我的生活也没多大改变。

sentences.en: And honestly, I just felt like I was falling behind.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我就是觉得自己在落后。

sentences.en: In college, I tried so many different things because I always had this dream of doing something creative.
sentences.zh: 大学期间我试了无数东西，因为我一直有个梦想，想做创造性的事。

sentences.en: But I was going to college, and if college ended and I didn't have a creative income source, then I would have to get a job.
sentences.zh: 但我当时在上大学，如果大学毕业了我还没有一个创造性的收入来源，那我就得去找工作。

sentences.en: And so it's like, I need to figure out what I need to do now.
sentences.zh: 所以情况就是，我必须现在就搞清楚自己该做什么。

sentences.en: And so I just experimented with a bunch of different things, but I didn't stick to one thing.
sentences.zh: 于是我就各种尝试，但没有一件事坚持下来。

sentences.en: And so that's what happened five years into college, one more year than I was supposed to go.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，大学上了五年，比正常多了一年。

sentences.en: I had to get a job because I just needed to survive, right?
sentences.zh: 我还是得去找工作，因为我得活下去，对吧？

sentences.en: I needed money, but the missing piece for me that I'm guessing is a missing piece for you was a vessel, a vessel, a way to channel your multiple interests into one thing.
sentences.zh: 我需要钱，但对我来说缺失的那一块——我猜对你来说也是——是一个载体，一个能把你多重兴趣汇聚到一件事上的载体。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: That's not what people consider a specialist to be.
sentences.zh: 那不是人们通常认为的专家。

sentences.en: That's more of a generalist. Right?
sentences.zh: 那更像一个通才。对吧？

sentences.en: The let's say the definition of a generalist is someone who has an aim for their life.
sentences.zh: 这么说吧，通才的定义是，一个对自己的人生有目标的人。

sentences.en: They have a desired outcome, they have a future they want to achieve, and they do all of the things required to achieve that.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个渴望达成的结果，有一个想要实现的未来，然后他们会去做实现那个未来所需的一切。

sentences.en: We're going to dig deeper into this, but that's such a huge insight that you may not understand yet.
sentences.zh: 我们会深入探讨这一点，但这可能是一个你还没理解的巨大洞见。

sentences.en: In other words, I needed to do something that could generate an income so that I could survive.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我需要做一件能产生收入的事，让我能活下去。

sentences.en: But it umbrella did all of my interests into it.
sentences.zh: 但这件事要像一把伞，把我所有的兴趣都涵盖进去。

sentences.en: So if you've ever felt guilty for not being able to pick one thing, if you've been told to niche down when your mind wants to expand, if you've wondered whether there's a path you can take that doesn't lead to the misery you see in everyone else's eyes, this is the greatest time to be alive.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你曾因为无法只选一件事而感到愧疚，如果你曾被要求“细分定位”而你的大脑却想要扩张，如果你曾怀疑是否存在一条路，不会通向你在别人眼中看到的那种痛苦——那现在就是最好的时代。

sentences.en: So here are the seven most compelling and practical ideas that I came up with.
sentences.zh: 以下是我总结的七个最有说服力、也最实用的想法。

sentences.en: For people with multiple interests, we'll start by understanding why having multiple interests is a superpower, which is very important.
sentences.zh: 对于拥有多重兴趣的人，我们先从理解为什么多重兴趣是一种超能力开始，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: And then I'll give you the practical steps, kind of hyper practical.
sentences.zh: 然后我会给你实操步骤，非常实操的那种。

sentences.en: This is kind of like a full course on how to turn those into your life's work.
sentences.zh: 这有点像一门完整的课程，教你如何把这些兴趣变成你一生的事业。

sentences.en: And this will especially make sense in my next video called The Future of Work, which is just going to be a huge synthesis of all the research I've done on what the future could look like with AI, AGI, etc. I think you'll like that, especially if you're a creative.
sentences.zh: 而这一切尤其会在我下一期叫《工作的未来》的视频里串联起来，那期会是我所有研究的巨大合成，关于AI、AGI等等可能带来的未来。我觉得你会喜欢的，尤其如果你是一个创造者。

sentences.en: So we have a lot to talk about.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要聊的很多。

sentences.en: I hope you're here for the right.
sentences.zh: 我希望你是为此而来的。

sentences.en: If you're not, just save this to watch later so it pops up again or something so you don't forget about it.
sentences.zh: 如果不是，就先存下来稍后观看，这样它会再弹出来，免得你忘了。

sentences.en: So the first idea we're going to talk about the three ingredients of individual success and the death of the expert.
sentences.zh: 那么第一个要聊的想法：个人成功的三个要素，以及专家的消亡。

sentences.en: And we'll start with a quote from Adam Smith, who had a huge influence on the birth of capitalism.
sentences.zh: 我们从亚当·斯密的一句话开始，他对资本主义的诞生有巨大影响。

sentences.en: We'll talk about that in a bit.
sentences.zh: 这个我们稍后会聊。

sentences.en: But the quote is, the man whose whole life is spent in performing a few simple operations generally becomes as stupid and ignorant as it is possible for a human creature to become.
sentences.zh: 这句话是：“一个人如果把一生都花在完成几个简单操作上，通常会变得愚蠢和无知，达到人类可能达到的极限。”

sentences.en: So it's funny that he says that because industrial age, capitalism, free markets, employment, etc. I'm not against capitalism.
sentences.zh: 他说这话挺有意思的，因为工业时代、资本主义、自由市场、雇佣制等等——我并不反对资本主义。

sentences.en: I think it's going to evolve into something better, hopefully.
sentences.zh: 我认为它会进化成更好的东西，希望如此。

sentences.en: But it's funny that he says that because he's the one who contributed to it, if not created it.
sentences.zh: 但他说这话很讽刺，因为他正是促成这一切的人，甚至可以说是他创造了它。

sentences.en: So specialization took over because in a pin factory, for example, this happened across many different types of factories and lines of work.
sentences.zh: 专业化之所以占据主导，是因为在一家别针工厂里——这发生在许多不同类型的工厂和工作领域——举个例子。

sentences.en: One worker doing every step could produce 20 pins a day, and then many workers, each doing one step rather than every step, could produce 48,000.
sentences.zh: 一个工人完成所有步骤，一天能生产20枚别针；而许多工人每人只做一个步骤，一天能生产48000枚。

sentences.en: So we built an entire world around this model.
sentences.zh: 于是我们围绕这个模型构建了整个世界。

sentences.en: We just siloed people into doing individual, repetitive robotic tasks.
sentences.zh: 我们只是把人塞进一个个孤岛，让他们去做孤立的、重复的、机器人般的任务。

sentences.en: And you can wonder why we're at threat of replacement from robots right now.
sentences.zh: 然后你就能明白，为什么我们现在面临被机器人取代的威胁。

sentences.en: It's because humans became assembly lines working 9 to 5 jobs.
sentences.zh: 因为人类自己变成了流水线，做着朝九晚五的工作。

sentences.en: And this happened because, frankly, governments don't serve the national interest, the interest of the people.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的发生，坦白说，是因为政府并不服务于国家利益、人民的利益。

sentences.en: They serve their own interest.
sentences.zh: 它们服务于自己的利益。

sentences.en: So the opposite of capitalism also isn't the answer, but the same thing applies here to corporations.
sentences.zh: 所以资本主义的反面也不是答案，但同样的道理也适用于企业。

sentences.en: The corporations don't serve the employees interests.
sentences.zh: 公司不为员工的利益服务。

sentences.en: They serve their own, and their own interest is profit.
sentences.zh: 它们为自己的利益服务，而它们的利益就是利润。

sentences.en: And since that starts to form the base of the economy and just the general culture of the US or the West, then schools were also designed to serve that interest.
sentences.zh: 当这一点开始构成经济基础，乃至整个美国或西方文化的基调时，学校也被设计来服务于这个利益。

sentences.en: Their sole purpose was to create factory workers who were obedient.
sentences.zh: 学校的唯一目的就是培养听话的工厂工人。

sentences.en: And the school system hasn't changed much.
sentences.zh: 而学校体系至今没怎么变过。

sentences.en: So if you want to have specialized knowledge so that you could never run an operation, especially your own operation, then be dependent on schools for your education and jobs for your wage.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想拥有专业技能，以至于永远无法运营一个事业，尤其是你自己的事业，那就依赖学校获取教育，依赖工作获取工资吧。

sentences.en: Be duped into believing that specialization is what makes a human valuable.
sentences.zh: 被蒙骗去相信专业化才是一个人价值的来源。

sentences.en: When it is clear that the system does not need you specifically to perform that task.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，那个系统并不需要你这个人去完成那个任务。

sentences.en: So in lies the distinction.
sentences.zh: 区别就在这里。

sentences.en: If specialization makes people stupid, then what makes someone free?
sentences.zh: 如果专业化让人变蠢，那什么让人自由？

sentences.en: What makes someone sovereign and there's three ingredients self-education, self-interest, and self-sufficiency.
sentences.zh: 什么让人拥有主权？有三个要素：自我教育、自身利益、自给自足。

sentences.en: So self education is pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 自我教育很好理解。

sentences.en: If you want a different result from the one that traditional education promises, then you must direct your own learning.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要一个不同于传统教育所承诺的结果，你就必须主导自己的学习。

sentences.en: Now, self-interest raises some flags because it sounds selfish and shortsighted, right?
sentences.zh: 自身利益这个词会让人警觉，因为它听起来自私又短视，对吧？

sentences.en: Everyone should be selfless.
sentences.zh: 每个人都应该无私。

sentences.en: That's what you've been told.
sentences.zh: 你一直被这样教导。

sentences.en: But self-interest simply means concerned with one's own interest.
sentences.zh: 但自身利益的意思很简单，就是关心自己的利益。

sentences.en: And if that isn't a priority for you, then whose interest are you going to serve?
sentences.zh: 如果这对你来说都不是优先事项，那你打算去服务谁的利益？

sentences.en: Especially when your survival is dependent on it.
sentences.zh: 尤其当你的生存都依赖它的时候。

sentences.en: You're going to serve the interest of the schools, the jobs and the government, and those interests are not very beneficial to you.
sentences.zh: 你会去服务学校、工作和政府的利益，而这些利益对你并没有多大好处。

sentences.en: In other words, you need to follow your own interest because your interest is often beneficial to others.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你需要追随自己的兴趣，因为你的兴趣往往对他人也有益。

sentences.en: And of course, this depends on what level of cognitive development that you're at.
sentences.zh: 当然，这取决于你处在哪个认知发展阶段。

sentences.en: But I would assume that most people don't want to hurt most people.
sentences.zh: 但我相信大多数人并不想伤害大多数人。

sentences.en: And I would assume that in the culture and day and age that we live in, most people are beyond that end.
sentences.zh: 我也相信，在我们所处的文化和时代，大多数人已经超越了那个阶段。

sentences.en: An objection or argument here is that, well, if I were if people just served their own interests, then they would just be scrolling on their phones all day and all and indulging in cheap pleasures and dopamine and gambling and all this other stuff.
sentences.zh: 这里可能会有一个反对意见：如果人们只服务于自身利益，那他们岂不是整天刷手机，沉溺于廉价快感、多巴胺、赌博之类的东西。

sentences.en: But take take a second and look, whose interest does that actually serve?
sentences.zh: 但你停下来想一想，那到底是在服务谁的利益？

sentences.en: That is usually not your actual interest, but an interest that you have become addicted to, or an interest that's been assigned to you.
sentences.zh: 那通常不是你真正的利益，而是你已上瘾的利益，或者被分配给你的利益。

sentences.en: And that's usually comes from the corporations who actually own the social media companies that you're scrolling on each and every day, getting sucked into the algorithm and not curating or being intentional about your own feed.
sentences.zh: 这通常来自那些公司，它们拥有你每天都在刷的社交媒体平台，让你被算法吞噬，而不是去精心策划、有意识地管理自己的信息流。

sentences.en: And I'll let you think through the rest.
sentences.zh: 剩下的你自己去想。

sentences.en: Now, the truly selfish person, in Ayn Rand's view, is a self-respecting, self-supporting human being who neither sacrifices others to himself nor sacrifices himself to others.
sentences.zh: 在安·兰德看来，真正自私的人，是一个自尊、自立的人，既不牺牲他人来成全自己，也不牺牲自己去成全他人。

sentences.en: This rejects both the predator and the doormat.
sentences.zh: 这同时拒绝了掠夺者和受气包两种角色。

sentences.en: So that's self-interest. And now self-sufficiency.
sentences.zh: 这就是自身利益。现在来说自给自足。

sentences.en: The last ingredient is the refusal to outsource your judgment, your learning, and your agency.
sentences.zh: 最后一个要素是拒绝外包你的判断力、你的学习和你的自主权。

sentences.en: So if self-education is the engine and self-interest is the compass, then self-sufficiency is the foundation that prevents your life direction from being hijacked.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果自我教育是引擎，自身利益是指南针，那么自给自足就是地基，防止你的人生方向被劫持。

sentences.en: So the generalist naturally must emerge.
sentences.zh: 所以通才必然会涌现出来。

sentences.en: Someone with multiple interests must emerge if they fit into this triad or they develop this triad of traits.
sentences.zh: 一个拥有多重兴趣的人，只要符合这三要素，或者发展出这三要素，就必然会涌现出来。

sentences.en: Because self-interest motivates self-education.
sentences.zh: 因为自我兴趣会驱动自我教育。

sentences.en: You learn things because it genuinely improves your life.
sentences.zh: 你学东西，是因为它真的能改善你的生活。

sentences.en: You're not assigned to learn things for the interest of the system that you're within.
sentences.zh: 你不是被指派去学那些为你所在系统利益服务的东西。

sentences.en: And then self-education enables self-sufficiency because you can only be as sovereign as the domains you understand.
sentences.zh: 而自我教育又能促成自给自足，因为你只能在你自己理解的领域里拥有主权。

sentences.en: And if you're a specialist, you wonder, you only understand one domain.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个专才，你只理解一个领域。

sentences.en: There's a reason you can't run the entire operation and why you're kept dumb to that.
sentences.zh: 你无法运营整个业务是有原因的，你被刻意蒙在鼓里也是有原因的。

sentences.en: And you're kept siloed. Because actually, think about it.
sentences.zh: 你被关在孤岛里。你仔细想想。

sentences.en: If you knew how to run the entire company, it was very clear to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道怎么运营整个公司，这件事对你来说一清二楚。

sentences.en: You understood it. You knew how to do it.
sentences.zh: 你理解它，你知道怎么做。

sentences.en: Then why wouldn't you do that?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么不去做呢？

sentences.en: And last, that self-sufficiency clarifies your self-interest.
sentences.zh: 最后，自给自足会反过来澄清你的自我兴趣。

sentences.en: So it's like a cycle.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像一个循环。

sentences.en: It's a it's a triad, but it's also a cycle.
sentences.zh: 它是一个三要素结构，同时也是一个循环。

sentences.en: Because when you're not dependent on others interpretations, you can actually perceive what serves you.
sentences.zh: 因为当你不依赖他人的解读时，你才能真正感知到什么对你有益。

sentences.en: Most people pursue multiple interests as an escape from their work.
sentences.zh: 大多数人追求多重兴趣，只是为了逃避工作。

sentences.en: But when your interests become your work or your life's work, most of them start to filter out.
sentences.zh: 但当你的兴趣变成了你的工作，或者你一生的事业，大部分兴趣就会开始被过滤掉。

sentences.en: So you think you have all of these, interests that may not lead to something beneficial monetarily or in terms of money.
sentences.zh: 所以你以为自己有一大堆兴趣，可能不会带来什么金钱上的收益。

sentences.en: But once you actually get on the path, when work turns into play for you, then you tend to drop the interest that just served as an escape, and you really start to focus in and clarify what you want out of life.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你真正走上这条路，当工作对你来说变成了玩，你就会开始丢掉那些只用来逃避的兴趣，真正聚焦并澄清你到底想要从人生中得到什么。

sentences.en: So you may have too many interests right now, but once you actually start to get on the right path, as we're going to discuss, they will become so much more clear.
sentences.zh: 所以你现在可能兴趣太多，但一旦你真正开始走上正确的路——我们接下来会讨论——它们会变得清晰得多。

sentences.en: That is the best way to manage multiple interests.
sentences.zh: 这是管理多重兴趣最好的方式。

sentences.en: I see these videos on how to manage multiple interests from accounts that I like.
sentences.zh: 我看到一些我喜欢的账号发过关于如何管理多重兴趣的视频。

sentences.en: Odysseus, I love you, but I don't think those people are on the right track.
sentences.zh: Odysseus，我很喜欢你，但我不认为那些人走对了路。

sentences.en: I don't think creating a note taking system as someone with a note taking software, I don't think creating the note taking system to manage all of these notes and other things that don't serve any higher goal in your life, even if it's not directly tied to money.
sentences.zh: 我不认为作为一个笔记软件用户，去创建一个笔记系统来管理所有笔记和其他东西，能服务于你人生中任何更高的目标，即使它跟钱没有直接关系。

sentences.en: But if money is a currency of agency expressing your agency, then money is important because that allows you to discover something more meaningful and to choose that meaningful thing over the options that are available to you right now in a culture that glorifies productivity as God.
sentences.zh: 但如果金钱是表达你自主权的货币，那钱就是重要的，因为它能让你发现更有意义的东西，并让你在当下这个把生产力奉为神的文化里，去选择那个有意义的东西，而不是被眼前的选择困住。

sentences.en: So to prevent a rant, let's get back on track.
sentences.zh: 为了避免跑题太久，我们回到正轨。

sentences.en: When you look at every CEO or creative or founder, they're almost always a generalist, even if it doesn't seem like it on the surface because they understand enough about marketing to direct it, enough about product to build it, and enough about people to lead them.
sentences.zh: 你看看每一个CEO、创作者或创始人，他们几乎都是通才，即使表面上看不出来，因为他们懂足够的营销去指导方向，懂足够的产品去构建它，懂足够的人去领导他们。

sentences.en: But they also need to direct the ship.
sentences.zh: 但他们还需要掌舵。

sentences.en: They need to learn and adapt.
sentences.zh: 他们需要学习和适应。

sentences.en: When circumstances change, meaning they have to learn a lot and they have to go very broad.
sentences.zh: 当环境变化时，意味着他们必须学很多东西，必须走得很广。

sentences.en: They can't go too deep on one thing aside from their company, but that has its own benefits.
sentences.zh: 除了自己的公司，他们不能在任何单一事情上钻得太深，但这本身也有好处。

sentences.en: It has the benefit of creating your own unique model of the world, your own unique way of viewing the world.
sentences.zh: 好处就是创造出你自己独特的世界模型，你自己独特的看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: Because ideas that cross into different domains, they compliment each other and that unique way of viewing the world allows you to catch and see ideas and opportunities that other people wouldn't see.
sentences.zh: 因为跨越不同领域的想法会相互补充，而这种独特的看待世界的方式，能让你捕捉到别人看不到的想法和机会。

sentences.en: So it's harder to replicate until you actually put in the work of building it, and then someone can try to replicate it, but they don't. They still don't have the unique way of viewing the world.
sentences.zh: 所以它很难被复制，直到你真的投入功夫把它构建出来，然后别人可以尝试复制，但他们做不到。他们仍然没有那种看待世界的独特方式。

sentences.en: They still don't have all of the intersections of ideas that led to the specific decision making that you made.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然没有那些想法的交叉点，那些交叉点引导你做出了特定的决策。

sentences.en: So you are much more likely to succeed than them.
sentences.zh: 所以你比他们更有可能成功。

sentences.en: That leads into idea number two, which is that you are living through the Second Renaissance, and you need to take advantage of it.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第二个想法：你正活在第二次文艺复兴中，你需要抓住这个机会。

sentences.en: So another quote from Da Vinci study the science of art.
sentences.zh: 再引用一句达·芬奇的话：研究艺术的科学。

sentences.en: Study the art of science.
sentences.zh: 研究科学的艺术。

sentences.en: Develop your senses, especially learn how to see.
sentences.zh: 发展你的感官，尤其是学会如何去看。

sentences.en: Realize that everything connects to everything else.
sentences.zh: 认识到万事万物都彼此相连。

sentences.en: The ultimate moat or the final competitive advantage worth paying for, in my opinion, is an opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，终极的护城河，或者说最后那个值得付费的竞争优势，是一种观点。

sentences.en: It is a perspective that only you can see because the uniqueness of your life experience created it.
sentences.zh: 它是一种只有你才能看到的视角，因为你独特的人生经历创造了它。

sentences.en: That may just be the last thing anyone else can replicate.
sentences.zh: 那可能是任何人都无法复制的最后一样东西。

sentences.en: And since that's always been the case, that's always been the case.
sentences.zh: 而既然这一直都是事实，这一直都是事实。

sentences.en: You have to understand that that has always been the case.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，这一直都是事实。

sentences.en: Why not prioritize it now, especially when automation is at your doorstep?
sentences.zh: 为什么不现在就把它放在首位，尤其是当自动化已经来到你家门口的时候？

sentences.en: This is like forcing everyone to prioritize the one thing that has mattered and will matter.
sentences.zh: 这就像是在强迫每个人去优先考虑那件一直重要、未来也重要的事。

sentences.en: But how do you prioritize it?
sentences.zh: 但你如何把它放在首位？

sentences.en: How do you develop it?
sentences.zh: 你如何发展它？

sentences.en: By pursuing multiple interests and building something with them.
sentences.zh: 通过追求多种兴趣，并用它们去构建一些东西。

sentences.en: Actually, it's the reverse.
sentences.zh: 实际上，是反过来的。

sentences.en: By building something useful and learning the multiple interests that you have to learn.
sentences.zh: 通过构建一些有用的东西，并学习你不得不学的多种兴趣。

sentences.en: Because every interest you've ever pursued leaves behind a residue.
sentences.zh: 因为你追求过的每一个兴趣都会留下残留物。

sentences.en: Every interest increases the number of connections that can be made.
sentences.zh: 每一个兴趣都会增加你能建立的联系的数量。

sentences.en: Every interest expands and increases the complexity of how you model and interpret reality.
sentences.zh: 每一个兴趣都会扩展并增加你建模和解读现实的复杂度。

sentences.en: And the more complex your model of reality, the more problems you can solve, opportunities you can see and value, you can create.
sentences.zh: 而你的现实模型越复杂，你就能解决越多问题，看到越多机会，创造越多价值。

sentences.en: Specialism completely halts this process and your shiny object syndrome has been trying to tell you this whole time, from birth until now.
sentences.zh: 专业化完全终止了这个过程，而你的"闪亮物体综合征"从出生到现在，一直在试图告诉你这一点。

sentences.en: Just think of how complex that is, right?
sentences.zh: 想想看这有多复杂，对吧？

sentences.en: We take advantage of just every single passing moment, every single thing that's happened to us all of the billions upon billions of bits of information that our mind has processed in our own unique location, situation, culture from the bottom up.
sentences.zh: 我们利用每一个流逝的瞬间，每一件发生在我们身上的事，我们头脑在自身独特的位置、处境、文化中自下而上处理过的数十亿计的信息。

sentences.en: There's so many different things influencing how we see the world throughout.
sentences.zh: 有太多不同的因素在影响着我们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: From birth until now, you have cultivated a way of seeing things that others cannot access.
sentences.zh: 从出生到现在，你培养出了一种别人无法触及的看待事物的方式。

sentences.en: I cannot think this way until you tell AI to think that way.
sentences.zh: 我无法这样思考，除非你告诉 AI 这样思考。

sentences.en: So a person who studied psychology and design sees user behavior differently from a pure designer.
sentences.zh: 所以一个学过心理学和设计的人，看待用户行为的方式与一个纯粹的设计师不同。

sentences.en: Now imagine if they tacked on something else to that.
sentences.zh: 现在想象一下，如果他们在那之上又叠加了别的东西。

sentences.en: Aside from just psychology and design, a person who learns sales and philosophy closes deals differently than the pure salesman.
sentences.zh: 除了心理学和设计，一个学过销售和哲学的人，成交的方式与纯粹的销售员不同。

sentences.en: A person who understands fitness and business built health companies that MBAs can't understand.
sentences.zh: 一个懂健身和商业的人，能打造出 MBA 们无法理解的健康公司。

sentences.en: And if you really think about it, this is the exact pattern that showed in the Renaissance in what allowed individuals to flourish.
sentences.zh: 如果你认真想一想，这正是文艺复兴时期显现出来的模式，正是这种模式让个体得以蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: So we have to consider what made that possible and see if that shows up today, which it does.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须思考是什么让这一切成为可能，再看看今天是否也出现了同样的条件——答案是，确实出现了。

sentences.en: So before the printing press, knowledge was scarce, books were copied by hand in a single text could take a scribe months to reproduce.
sentences.zh: 在印刷机出现之前，知识是稀缺的，书籍靠手抄，一本著作可能要抄写员花几个月才能复制出来。

sentences.en: Libraries were very rare and literacy was rare.
sentences.zh: 图书馆极其罕见，识字率也很低。

sentences.en: If you wanted to learn something outside of your trade, you either had access to a monastery or you didn't learn that thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你想学点本行之外的东西，要么你能进修道院，要么你就根本学不到。

sentences.en: And then Gutenberg changed everything.
sentences.zh: 然后古腾堡改变了一切。

sentences.en: So within 50 years, 20 million books flooded Europe, ideas that once took generations to spread, now moved in months, literacy exploded.
sentences.zh: 不到五十年，两千万本书涌入欧洲，曾经需要几代人才能传播的思想，现在几个月就传开了，识字率爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: The cost of knowledge collapsed.
sentences.zh: 知识的成本断崖式下跌。

sentences.en: For the first time in history, a person could realistically pursue multiple domains of mastery in a single lifetime, and the Renaissance was the result.
sentences.zh: 有史以来第一次，一个人真的有可能在一生中精通多个领域，文艺复兴就是结果。

sentences.en: So whenever someone compares this to AI, they say, oh well, it's not the same.
sentences.zh: 所以每当有人拿这个来类比 AI，他们就说，哦，这不一样。

sentences.en: An AI does so much more, but the pattern is still there.
sentences.zh: AI 能做的事多得多，但那个模式依然存在。

sentences.en: There is still something there.
sentences.zh: 那里依然有某种东西。

sentences.en: And I don't think anyone has figured out what the future is going to look like yet because it's just prediction, it's speculation, it's imaginary.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为有人已经搞清楚未来会是什么样子，因为那只是预测、只是推测、只是想象。

sentences.en: So it's worthwhile to at least hold these ideas in your mind without accepting them as truth, but potentially pursuing them or utilizing these ideas because they can be useful to your life right now and probably going into the future.
sentences.zh: 所以至少把这些想法放在脑子里是有价值的，不必当作真理接受，但可以试着去追寻或运用这些想法，因为它们对你现在的生活有用，而且很可能对未来也有用。

sentences.en: It's better than doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 这总比什么都不做强。

sentences.en: When we look at Da Vinci, he didn't just do one thing.
sentences.zh: 我们看看达·芬奇，他并不是只做一件事。

sentences.en: He painted, sculpted, engineered, studied anatomy, designed war machines, and mapped the human body.
sentences.zh: 他画画、雕塑、搞工程、研究解剖学、设计战争机器、绘制人体图谱。

sentences.en: Michelangelo was a painter, sculptor, architect and poet.
sentences.zh: 米开朗基罗是画家、雕塑家、建筑师，也是诗人。

sentences.en: So in today's world, unique minds are finally able to operate the way they were meant to.
sentences.zh: 所以在今天的世界，独特的头脑终于可以按照它们本该有的方式运作。

sentences.en: They were supposed to cross disciplines, synthesize connection, and follow curiosity.
sentences.zh: 它们本就该跨越学科、综合关联、追随好奇心。

sentences.en: Wherever it led.
sentences.zh: 无论好奇心通向哪里。

sentences.en: The printing press was a catalyst for a new type of person to emerge.
sentences.zh: 印刷机是一种催化剂，催生了一种新型人类的出现。

sentences.en: A person who could learn anything, combine everything, and create something that no specialist ever could.
sentences.zh: 这种人什么都能学，什么都能融合，能创造出任何专才都无法创造的东西。

sentences.en: And this is happening again.
sentences.zh: 而这一切正在再次发生。

sentences.en: So idea number three, how to turn multiple interests into a lucrative way of life.
sentences.zh: 所以第三个想法：如何把多重兴趣变成一种能赚钱的生活方式。

sentences.en: So as a recap, there are few things that we know so far.
sentences.zh: 先回顾一下，我们目前已知的有这么几点。

sentences.en: You have multiple interests, but feel like you can't keep learning forever.
sentences.zh: 你有多重兴趣，但觉得不可能永远学下去。

sentences.en: You have a love for interest based self-education, but have to carve out time outside of your career to do it.
sentences.zh: 你热爱基于兴趣的自我教育，但不得不在主业之外挤出时间来做这件事。

sentences.en: You understand the need to become self-sufficient, but you feel like you don't have value worth paying for yet, and you need to be able to adapt fast because we don't know what the future looks like.
sentences.zh: 你明白自己需要变得自给自足，但又觉得自己还没有值得别人付费的价值，而且你必须能够快速适应，因为我们不知道未来会是什么样。

sentences.en: So the question then is, how do we combine all of these things or all of our interests into a way of life, not a way of work life balance, but a complete way of life, a way of turning work into play.
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了：我们如何把所有这些、把我们所有的兴趣，融合成一种生活方式——不是工作生活平衡，而是一种完整的生活方式，一种把工作变成玩的方式。

sentences.en: So I'll try to make this as logical as I can and just boom, boom, boom, tie these things together to make money from your interests.
sentences.zh: 所以我尽量讲得逻辑清晰一点，直接 boom boom boom 把这些东西串起来，让你能用兴趣赚钱。

sentences.en: You need other people to become interested in them too.
sentences.zh: 你需要让其他人也对你的兴趣产生兴趣。

sentences.en: That part is trivial because if you became interested in something other people can too, you simply must learn to persuade.
sentences.zh: 这部分其实很简单，因为如果你能对某件事产生兴趣，别人也能，你只需要学会说服。

sentences.en: So skill to learn, right their persuasion.
sentences.zh: 所以要去学的技能，对，就是说服。

sentences.en: Just read a few books on persuasion and it'll naturally catch on.
sentences.zh: 读几本关于说服力的书，自然就上手了。

sentences.en: If you are creating something with that, you need a way for these people to pay you.
sentences.zh: 如果你在用这些东西创作，你需要一个让这些人付钱给你的方式。

sentences.en: In this context, that usually means you need to sell a product, because you probably aren't going to find a job that allows you to express your interest in investing in stocks or real estate to any effective degree, requires a good amount of capital.
sentences.zh: 在这个语境下，通常意味着你得卖一个产品，因为你大概率找不到一份工作，能让你有效表达你对股票或房地产投资的兴趣，那需要大量资本。

sentences.en: So in other words, you need attention.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你需要注意力。

sentences.en: Attention is one of the last moats because it's very scarce.
sentences.zh: 注意力是仅存的护城河之一，因为它非常稀缺。

sentences.en: Scarcity is going to survive right?
sentences.zh: 稀缺的东西才能活下来，对吧？

sentences.en: AGI can't make attention a commodity.
sentences.zh: AGI 没法把注意力变成一种商品。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It can provide maybe in the future a basic foundation for survival.
sentences.zh: 未来它也许能提供一个基本的生存基础。

sentences.en: Right. We don't have to worry about survival anymore.
sentences.zh: 对，我们不用再担心生存问题了。

sentences.en: The things that we see is scarce right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的稀缺的东西。

sentences.en: A lot of the things will become commodities.
sentences.zh: 很多东西都会变成商品。

sentences.en: But our attention, there's only so much to go around.
sentences.zh: 但我们的注意力，总量就那么多。

sentences.en: So what's worth paying for in the future?
sentences.zh: 所以未来什么才值得付费？

sentences.en: And as a creative, you may be surprised to hear this, but it's creative work.
sentences.zh: 作为一个创作者，你听了可能会惊讶，但答案是创造性工作。

sentences.en: Stop worrying about AI copying your image or copying your writing.
sentences.zh: 别再担心 AI 复制你的图片或复制你的文字了。

sentences.en: We'll talk about this more in I think it's the next video.
sentences.zh: 这个我们后面再聊，应该是下一期视频。

sentences.en: Just think about it.
sentences.zh: 你想想看。

sentences.en: If anyone can write anything or build anything or create anything like we're hearing right now, especially if you're on Twitter, it's frickin everywhere and I don't disagree with them.
sentences.zh: 如果任何人都能写任何东西、做任何东西、创造任何东西，就像我们现在听到的那样，尤其是你在 Twitter 上，这种论调到处都是，我并不反对他们。

sentences.en: Anyone's going to be able to create anything which ones are going to win.
sentences.zh: 任何人都能创造任何东西，那谁会赢？

sentences.en: It's going to be the ones that people know about.
sentences.zh: 赢的是那些人们知道的东西。

sentences.en: It's the ones that people pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 是那些人们给予注意力的东西。

sentences.en: Because you can have the greatest product in the world.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以拥有世界上最好的产品。

sentences.en: You can have your greatest little mobile app or SAS app, but if nobody knows about it, it just ends up like every single other product or SAS app that's been created in the past that nobody knows about, it just doesn't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你可以有最棒的小型移动应用或 SaaS 应用，但如果没人知道它，它最终就跟过去所有那些没人知道的、被创造出来的产品或 SaaS 应用一样，根本走不远。

sentences.en: You you didn't waste your time.
sentences.zh: 你并没有浪费你的时间。

sentences.en: You learn some stuff.
sentences.zh: 你学到了一些东西。

sentences.en: Maybe, but you're missing a piece of the puzzle.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，但你缺了拼图的一块。

sentences.en: It's never only just been build this thing, it's so much more than that.
sentences.zh: 从来都不只是“把这个东西做出来”，远不止如此。

sentences.en: And the other thing here is just opinionated work.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，就是有观点的作品。

sentences.en: Opinionated creative work.
sentences.zh: 有观点的创造性工作。

sentences.zh: 你更愿意用这个 vibe coded 的 SaaS 应用吗？比如一个 Dropbox 替代品，它没有一个能处理数十亿用户的大团队来维护？

sentences.en: Are you going to trust that with your.
sentences.zh: 你会把你的……托付给它吗？

sentences.zh: 而且你真的懂软件这个领域吗？
