sentences.zh: 我以前也不懂，直到我开始和我的团队一起做一个类似 Dropbox 替代品的东西。

sentences.en: But you're acting like people care a ton about the money that they spend on a useful solution in their life, and like, they even want to build that thing.
sentences.zh: 但你现在表现得好像人们特别在意花在一个有用方案上的那点钱，好像他们甚至想自己去搭那个东西。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't even spend 20 minutes cooking your own food every day for health and nutrition.
sentences.zh: 说真的，你连每天花20分钟给自己做顿健康营养的饭都做不到。

sentences.en: You pay 20 to 30 bucks for Uber Eats to deliver you food.
sentences.zh: 你花二三十美元让Uber Eats给你送餐。

sentences.en: Humans just want convenience on so many different levels and like people are blowing this way out of proportion as to what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 人类在很多层面上就是想要便利，大家把未来会发生的事想得太夸张了。

sentences.en: People have more things that they want to spend their time on, not everyone in the world just wants to be inside of cloud code building, like whatever suits their needs that day.
sentences.zh: 人们有更多想花时间去做的事，不是全世界每个人都想整天泡在Claude Code里搭东西，满足自己当天的需求。

sentences.en: Some people will, of course, but not even close to everyone.
sentences.zh: 当然会有一些人这么做，但远不是所有人。

sentences.en: So back to the point you need to become a creator now before you cringe and leave.
sentences.zh: 所以回到重点，你得趁自己还没尴尬到关掉视频之前，先成为一个创作者。

sentences.en: I don't necessarily mean become a content creator, even though I kind of do, but let's just unpack that.
sentences.zh: 我不一定是说成为内容创作者，虽然我差不多就是这个意思，但咱们先展开聊聊。

sentences.en: I mean that the solution to stop creating for someone else because you need them to give you a paycheck is to create for yourself humans by nature, are creators who are convinced that being a machine would lead to the American dream.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，停止为别人创造——因为你依赖他们给你发工资——而是开始为自己创造。人类天生就是创造者，只是被洗脑了，以为当一颗螺丝钉就能实现美国梦。

sentences.en: We are tool builders at our core.
sentences.zh: 我们骨子里是工具制造者。

sentences.en: We thrive in any niche because we create solutions to problems.
sentences.zh: 我们在任何领域都能活得很好，因为我们能为问题创造解决方案。

sentences.en: If a lion were put in Alaska, it would not build shelter and clothing, it would die.
sentences.zh: 如果把一头狮子放到阿拉斯加，它不会搭庇护所、不会做衣服，它会死。

sentences.en: A lion belongs in its own niche.
sentences.zh: 狮子属于它自己的生态位。

sentences.en: We don't belong in one niche.
sentences.zh: 我们不属于某一个生态位。

sentences.en: Everyone's telling you the niche down.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在跟你说要细分、要聚焦。

sentences.en: When everyone lives in a separate frickin niche across the world, it doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 当全世界每个人都活在各自不同的细分领域里，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Now, the second thing is that every business is a media business right now.
sentences.zh: 好，第二件事：现在每一家企业都是媒体企业。

sentences.en: And remember, you need attention.
sentences.zh: 记住，你需要注意力。

sentences.en: How do you generate attention? Media?
sentences.zh: 你怎么获取注意力？媒体。

sentences.en: Where is media?
sentences.zh: 媒体在哪？

sentences.en: Where is attention? Social media?
sentences.zh: 注意力在哪？社交媒体。

sentences.en: And that's at least right now things evolve, right?
sentences.zh: 至少目前是这样，事情会演变，对吧？

sentences.en: Social media platforms may not last forever, but something is going to take their place.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体平台可能不会永远存在，但会有别的东西取代它们。

sentences.en: And of course you're going to have to adapt at that point.
sentences.zh: 到那时候你当然得去适应。

sentences.en: So yes, if you have multiple interests, it would be wise in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，如果你有多个兴趣，在我看来这么做是明智的。

sentences.en: I don't want to just give a blanket prescription everyone, but it's so unique.
sentences.zh: 我不想给所有人开一张通用处方，每个人的情况太独特了。

sentences.en: You should probably become a content creator.
sentences.zh: 你大概应该成为一个内容创作者。

sentences.en: But you you also have to really think through how saturation just does not exist in this way.
sentences.zh: 但你也得真正想清楚，饱和根本不是这么回事。

sentences.en: There's no saturation in you meeting people in real life, right?
sentences.zh: 你在现实生活中认识人，这件事有饱和吗？没有吧。

sentences.en: There's there's a certain amount of people that you can have as close friends.
sentences.zh: 你能拥有的密友数量是有限的。

sentences.en: There's less people that you can have as friends.
sentences.zh: 你能拥有的朋友数量更少。

sentences.en: I mean, more people that you can have as friends.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能拥有的朋友数量更多。

sentences.en: And there's more people you can have as acquaintances.
sentences.zh: 你能拥有的泛泛之交数量更多。

sentences.en: There's more people that you can have as people you've met before.
sentences.zh: 你能拥有的"见过一面的人"数量更多。

sentences.en: And if you think of your consumption habits, you probably skim past hundreds of posts a day, potentially more.
sentences.zh: 你再想想自己的消费习惯，一天可能滑过几百条帖子，甚至更多。

sentences.en: What about long form, which takes longer to create?
sentences.zh: 那长内容呢？创作起来更花时间的那种。

sentences.en: Meaning that that decreases saturation even more?
sentences.zh: 这意味着饱和程度更低，对吧？

sentences.en: You maybe read one a day to a day.
sentences.zh: 你一天可能也就读个一篇。

sentences.en: How many YouTube videos do you watch a day for?
sentences.zh: 你一天看几个 YouTube 视频？

sentences.en: Five.
sentences.zh: 五个。

sentences.en: That's a lot of attention to go around.
sentences.zh: 这就有很多注意力可以分配了。

sentences.en: And how many videos do you skip?
sentences.zh: 而你跳过了多少个视频？

sentences.en: How many social post do you skip?
sentences.zh: 你又跳过了多少条社交帖子？

sentences.en: That just shows that there's an attention deficit.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰说明存在注意力赤字。

sentences.en: Not that your attention should just be in front of a screen all day, but also most of what you consume just sucks, right?
sentences.zh: 不是说你的注意力就该整天盯着屏幕，而是你消费的大部分内容真的很烂，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not good content.
sentences.zh: 不是好内容。

sentences.en: It's not beneficial to you.
sentences.zh: 对你没有益处。

sentences.en: It's not helping you learn.
sentences.zh: 帮不了你学习。

sentences.en: It's not providing anything meaningful.
sentences.zh: 提供不了任何有意义的东西。

sentences.en: There's a massive deficit of valuable and beneficial and useful content because you just look at your screen, look at what you're consuming every day.
sentences.zh: 有价值、有好处、有用的内容存在巨大的赤字，你只要看看自己的屏幕，看看自己每天在消费什么就知道了。

sentences.en: There's maybe 1 or 2 things, if that, that actually change your life.
sentences.zh: 真正能改变你生活的东西，可能也就一两样，甚至没有。

sentences.en: Not that you need to change your life all the time that are actually beneficial to you.
sentences.zh: 不是说你需要一直改变生活，而是说真正对你有益的东西太少了。

sentences.en: Now, if you don't like the idea of becoming a content creator, just think of social media as a mechanism to do independent work.
sentences.zh: 如果你不喜欢成为内容创作者这个想法，那就把社交媒体当成一个做独立工作的机制。

sentences.en: Because when we think about that, that covers all of our bases.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们这样想的时候，所有基础都覆盖到了。

sentences.en: If you love learning, great, reframe it as research.
sentences.zh: 如果你热爱学习，太好了，把它重新定义为研究。

sentences.en: And now that's literally your main job.
sentences.zh: 现在这基本上就是你的主要工作。

sentences.en: Most of the things I write about simply come from me learning about my interests and treating social media like I'm taking notes in public.
sentences.zh: 我写的大部分东西，都来自我学习自己感兴趣的东西，然后把社交媒体当成公开记笔记的地方。

sentences.en: So you're already spending time learning now just spend that time learning in public and boom, you have the foundation of a business.
sentences.zh: 你本来就已经在花时间学习，现在只要把学习变成公开的，砰，你就有了一人企业的基础。

sentences.en: If you need to become self-sufficient, well, you need a business to do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要自给自足，那你就需要一个生意来实现。

sentences.en: And every business needs to attract customers.
sentences.zh: 而每个生意都需要吸引客户。

sentences.en: And you probably don't give two fucks about paid ads, SEO, or any other form of marketing.
sentences.zh: 你可能根本不在乎付费广告、SEO 或任何其他营销方式。

sentences.en: This is what trips many people up because they are only used to doing one specialized task within a business.
sentences.zh: 这就是很多人卡住的地方，因为他们只习惯在生意里做一个专业化的任务。

sentences.en: As an employee, if you need to be able to adapt going to the future, which you do, then amazing!
sentences.zh: 作为一个员工，如果你需要适应未来——而你真的需要——那太棒了！

sentences.en: You can build and launch new products to your audience as fast as you can build them.
sentences.zh: 你可以向你的受众构建和发布新产品，速度有多快就能做多快。

sentences.en: I personally have a pretty solid audience and if my next product were to fail, I have people who would be willing to invest or work on the team, or even just support the next product.
sentences.zh: 我个人有相当稳固的受众，如果我的下一个产品失败了，我有人愿意投资、加入团队，甚至只是支持下一个产品。

sentences.en: It's not just one and done.
sentences.zh: 这不是一锤子买卖。

sentences.en: You don't just bust your entire load in one go on one launch, and if it fails, then all you're done.
sentences.zh: 你不是一次发布就把全部家当押上去，失败了就彻底完蛋。

sentences.en: It doesn't even cost you money to post content if you're.
sentences.zh: 发布内容甚至不花你一分钱，如果你——

sentences.en: Yeah, if you blew your life savings on paid ads, then maybe you're at a dead end.
sentences.zh: 对，如果你把毕生积蓄都砸在付费广告上，那你可能确实走进了死胡同。

sentences.en: But this is different, and it goes back to the point of you can build your little vibe coded SaaS company, and it may be very valuable.
sentences.zh: 但这是两码事，这又回到那个观点：你可以构建你的小 vibe coded SaaS 公司，它可能非常有价值。

sentences.en: I'm not denying that they can be valuable, but if you don't have distribution or an audience, then you're going to be putting in like a marathon's worth of effort into getting capital for it, into getting customers or users into finding talent and everything else that goes into building the business.
sentences.zh: 我不否认它们可以很有价值，但如果你没有分发渠道或受众，那你就要像跑马拉松一样拼命去搞资金、搞客户或用户、找人才，以及搞定构建业务所需的一切。

sentences.en: So my point is that no other job or career or path allows people with multiple interests to do all of those things.
sentences.zh: 所以我的观点是，没有任何其他工作、职业或路径，能让拥有多重兴趣的人同时做所有这些事。

sentences.en: So how do you actually start building it?
sentences.zh: 那你到底要怎么开始构建它？

sentences.en: Where's the practicality then?
sentences.zh: 实操在哪里？

sentences.en: What are the actionable steps I get you?
sentences.zh: 我给你可执行的步骤是什么？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Idea number four how to turn yourself into a business.
sentences.zh: 想法四：如何把自己变成一家企业。

sentences.en: Now, some of you have probably seen this graphic before on the one person business.
sentences.zh: 你们有些人可能之前看过这张关于一人企业的图。

sentences.en: I have an entire one person business playlist, but this has one less thing, right?
sentences.zh: 我有一整个一人企业的播放列表，但这张图少了一样东西，对吧？

sentences.en: So the three pillars, which used to be four pillars of a one person business, are brand, content and product.
sentences.zh: 一人企业过去是四大支柱，现在是三大支柱：品牌、内容和产品。

sentences.en: But how those differ from the traditional business is that your brand are your goals.
sentences.zh: 但它们与传统企业的区别在于，你的品牌就是你的目标。

sentences.en: So what do you want out of life?
sentences.zh: 你究竟想从生活中得到什么？

sentences.en: And then for brand, what are you helping people achieve for content or media or how you attract people to that brand?
sentences.zh: 然后对于品牌，你在帮助人们实现什么？对于内容或媒体，也就是你如何吸引人们到那个品牌，那就是知识。

sentences.en: That is knowledge.
sentences.zh: 那就是知识。

sentences.en: So what are you learning along the way and what is useful for them to know?
sentences.zh: 你在这个过程中学到了什么，什么对他们来说是有用的？

sentences.en: And then for product, which is process, how did you reach a desirable goal and how can you help them reach it faster.
sentences.zh: 然后是产品，也就是流程：你是如何达到一个理想目标的，以及你如何帮他们更快达到。

sentences.en: So let's break these down.
sentences.zh: 我们来拆解一下。

sentences.en: But first I'm talking to my younger self here.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我在对年轻的自己说话。

sentences.en: I'm talking to my younger self who was very, I guess, conditioned, very programed to have a negative outlook on money, a negative outlook on business, all these other things.
sentences.zh: 我在对年轻的自己说话，那个被严重规训、被深度编程，对金钱持负面看法、对企业持负面看法，以及所有这些东西的自己。

sentences.en: And it's really unfortunate that the words entrepreneurship and business have become kind of like dirty words that once someone hears them, they just shut off.
sentences.zh: 很不幸，“创业”和“商业”这些词已经变成了某种脏词，人们一听到就自动屏蔽。

sentences.en: It's like, no, I don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 就像，“不，我不想干那个。”

sentences.en: No, that's for unethical people.
sentences.zh: “不，那是给不道德的人干的。”

sentences.en: That's for talented people.
sentences.zh: “那是给有天赋的人干的。”

sentences.en: I'm not that talented.
sentences.zh: “我没那么有天赋。”

sentences.en: That's for people with a lot of money.
sentences.zh: “那是给有钱人干的。”

sentences.en: When that's that's just not the case on any grounds.
sentences.zh: 而这在任何层面上都不是事实。

sentences.en: The danger in doing that and closing your mind off to is that you're just closing your mind off to the thing that could change your life.
sentences.zh: 那样做、关闭你心智的危险在于，你只是对那件可能改变你人生的事情关闭了心智。

sentences.en: You're closing your mind off to the opportunities you're not able to see them.
sentences.zh: 你对那些机会关闭了心智，你无法看到它们。

sentences.en: If you reject the idea that allows you to see them.
sentences.zh: 如果你拒绝那个能让你看到它们的想法。

sentences.en: So my rebuttal to that is, if you've ever helped anyone with any of your interests in any way, then you are qualified to start a business.
sentences.zh: 所以我的反驳是：如果你曾用你的任何兴趣以任何方式帮助过任何人，那你就有资格创业。

sentences.en: It doesn't need to go any further than that.
sentences.zh: 不需要比这更进一步。

sentences.en: And the reality is that entrepreneurship is in our nature.
sentences.zh: 而现实是，创业精神就在我们的天性里。

sentences.en: It is modern survival.
sentences.zh: 这是现代版的生存。

sentences.en: We are wired to create and distribute value to a tribe of like minded people.
sentences.zh: 我们天生就会为一群志同道合的人创造和传递价值。

sentences.en: Now that tribe is on the internet and you have to find them or attract them.
sentences.zh: 现在这群人在互联网上，你得找到他们，或者吸引他们。

sentences.en: We are wired to hunt, to explore the unknown, to seek novelty and never stagnate.
sentences.zh: 我们天生就会狩猎、探索未知、寻求新奇，绝不原地踏步。

sentences.en: And psychologically, this is the most enjoyable way of life we've talked about that before, but if you study psychology and flow psychology, you will understand that and even further, the barrier of entry has collapsed.
sentences.zh: 从心理层面讲，这是我们聊过的最令人享受的生活方式。如果你研究心理学和心流心理学，你就会明白这一点。更进一步说，准入门槛已经崩塌了。

sentences.en: I'm not saying it's easy.
sentences.zh: 我不是说这很容易。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that you're just going to be able to go and talk to AI and have it spit out 30 posts, and then you posted on social media and instantly go viral and instantly see millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 我不是说你只要去跟AI聊几句，让它吐出30篇帖子，然后你往社交媒体上一发，就能瞬间爆火，瞬间看到几百万美元。

sentences.en: No, it's all skill based.
sentences.zh: 不，这一切都基于技能。

sentences.en: This is something that you're going to have to learn as well, but you're at an advantage because you love learning things.
sentences.zh: 这也是你必须学会的东西，但你有优势，因为你热爱学习。

sentences.en: It's still going to take time.
sentences.zh: 它仍然需要时间。

sentences.en: I don't care how fast AGI is going to speed up things, it still takes time to get any form of result in life.
sentences.zh: 我不管AGI会让事情加速多少，在生活中获得任何形式的成果都需要时间。

sentences.en: If you were to just get it immediately, then it would become a commodity and it'd be the same thing as you scrolling on your phone and it wouldn't bring any meaning to your life.
sentences.zh: 如果你能立刻得到，那它就会变成一种廉价品，跟你刷手机没什么两样，不会给你的生活带来任何意义。

sentences.en: So there are two paths that you can take when doing this one person business thing, or if it helps, just independent work or creating your life's work path.
sentences.zh: 所以，在做一人企业这件事上，或者说独立工作、创造你的人生作品，有两条路可以走。

sentences.en: One is skill based.
sentences.zh: 第一条，基于技能。

sentences.en: This is the typical way that people have been telling you to start a business for the longest time.
sentences.zh: 这是长久以来人们一直告诉你的那种典型创业方式。

sentences.en: I'm like, right, pick a marketable skill and then create a product or service around that marketable skill and you talk about that marketable skill online and then boom, you make money, I guess.
sentences.zh: 大概就是，选一个能变现的技能，然后围绕这个技能打造一个产品或服务，在网上聊这个技能，然后砰的一下，你就赚钱了，大概是这样。

sentences.en: But the limitation here is the limitation of being a specialist.
sentences.zh: 但这里的局限，就是成为专才的局限。

sentences.en: You probably don't want to be put into a box.
sentences.zh: 你可能不想被塞进一个盒子里。

sentences.en: You don't like feeling limited, but people do this.
sentences.zh: 你不喜欢被限制的感觉，但人们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: They niche down because they were told that was the most profitable thing to do.
sentences.zh: 他们细分定位，因为别人告诉他们这是最赚钱的做法。

sentences.en: And so now profit is your main interest.
sentences.zh: 于是现在，利润成了你的主要兴趣。

sentences.en: That's where everything else falls under.
sentences.zh: 其他一切都得服从于它。

sentences.en: That's your incentive.
sentences.zh: 那是你的驱动力。

sentences.en: So now that you're chasing profit, productivity is still your God.
sentences.zh: 所以既然你在追逐利润，生产力依然是你的神。

sentences.en: And you build yourself into a second 9 to 5 working on things you don't care about for people you don't care about.
sentences.zh: 你把自己活成了第二个朝九晚五，为你不关心的人，做你不关心的事。

sentences.en: So we're not going to talk about it beyond that, because that's not what we're here for.
sentences.zh: 所以这个话题我们到此为止，因为那不是我们今天要聊的。

sentences.en: So path number two is development based.
sentences.zh: 第二条路，基于发展。

sentences.en: And you can see this when you go into the creator economy.
sentences.zh: 你进入创作者经济时就能看到这一点。

sentences.en: Right now, if you're watching me, you probably watch other people that are on this path. You can observe it.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你在看我，你很可能也在看走这条路的人。你可以观察到。

sentences.en: And these people don't really have a niche that they're pinned down to write.
sentences.zh: 这些人并没有一个被钉死的细分定位。

sentences.en: In one video I talk about productivity.
sentences.zh: 在一个视频里我聊生产力。

sentences.en: In this video, I'm talking about business.
sentences.zh: 在这个视频里，我聊商业。

sentences.en: I guess I don't even know what it's like.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都不知道这算什么。

sentences.en: A combination of interests, the things that I learned this week really, or have learned over time.
sentences.zh: 一个兴趣的组合，是我这周真正学到的东西，或者说，是随时间积累学到的东西。

sentences.en: It's a synthesis of ideas with one overarching topic.
sentences.zh: 这是一种思想的综合，围绕一个统领性主题展开。

sentences.en: Now, typically what these people do is they focus on one of the four eternal markets and let their interest fall under those the eternal markets where all human problems tend to fall.
sentences.zh: 通常这类人会聚焦于四大永恒市场之一，让自己的兴趣归入这些市场之下——所有人类问题最终都会落在这几个领域。

sentences.en: So that's where all human value tends to fall.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有人类价值也都会落在这里。

sentences.en: What's valuable is health, wealth, relationships and happiness, or even all of them.
sentences.zh: 有价值的东西是健康、财富、关系和幸福，甚至涵盖全部。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You can bundle all of those things into the umbrella of self-actualization.
sentences.zh: 你可以把这些全部打包进自我实现这个总框架里。

sentences.en: I personally believe that most of the value creators online right now, they all have one niche.
sentences.zh: 我个人认为，现在线上大多数价值创造者，他们都有一个细分领域。

sentences.en: It's just a massive niche.
sentences.zh: 只不过是一个巨大的细分领域。

sentences.en: It's self-actualization.
sentences.zh: 那就是自我实现。

sentences.en: What makes it unique is how you reach self-actualization or even get close to it.
sentences.zh: 让它变得独特的是你如何抵达自我实现，甚至只是接近它。

sentences.en: You don't even have to get there.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不需要真的到达那里。

sentences.en: It's just your aim. It's what you're pursuing.
sentences.zh: 它只是你的目标，是你在追求的东西。

sentences.en: It's what you're helping other people do.
sentences.zh: 是你在帮助别人去做的事。

sentences.en: You document your journey there?
sentences.zh: 你记录自己走向那里的旅程。

sentences.en: You take notes that are disguised as ideas.
sentences.zh: 你写下那些伪装成想法的笔记。

sentences.en: Every single person that has the goal of self-transcendence or self-actualization, they're all taking infinitely unique paths to get there.
sentences.zh: 每一个以自我超越或自我实现为目标的人，都在走一条无限独特的路径。

sentences.en: And that's what matters.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键所在。

sentences.en: That's how you create a unique path.
sentences.zh: 这就是你创造独特路径的方式。

sentences.en: Someone who learns a skill, sells a marketable skill.
sentences.zh: 一个人学了一门技能，然后去卖一门可市场化的技能。

sentences.en: There's usually very little paths that you can take along that path.
sentences.zh: 那条路上通常没有太多路径可走。

sentences.en: So these types of creators, they pursue their own goals, which forms their brand.
sentences.zh: 所以这类创作者，他们追求自己的目标，这塑造了他们的品牌。

sentences.en: They teach what they learn, which forms their content, and they help others achieve the goal faster, which is their product.
sentences.zh: 他们教自己学到的东西，这构成了他们的内容；他们帮助别人更快达成目标，这就是他们的产品。

sentences.en: And the other powerful thing here is that when you take this path, you're the the first path.
sentences.zh: 这里另一个强大的地方在于，当你走上这条路，你就是第一条路径。

sentences.en: The skill based path is encapsulated in it.
sentences.zh: 基于技能的路径被包含在其中。

sentences.en: It's a natural part of it because you're building your own business, right?
sentences.zh: 它是自然而然的一部分，因为你在建立自己的一人企业，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to learn all of these things.
sentences.zh: 你必须学会所有这些事情。

sentences.en: You have to learn marketing, sales, brand, content, all of the little strategies you need to study these things, and you just become inherently valuable when you can do that, because you're learning the things that actually gets results.
sentences.zh: 你必须学会营销、销售、品牌、内容，以及研究这些所需的所有小策略。当你能做到这些时，你本身就变得极具价值，因为你在学习真正能拿到结果的东西。

sentences.en: Not all business owners do this.
sentences.zh: 并非所有企业主都这样做。

sentences.en: Go and talk to a small business and ask if they understand any of this. They don't. So if you learn it, you become valuable enough to be paid.
sentences.zh: 去找一个小企业主聊聊，问问他们是否理解这些。他们不理解。所以如果你学会了，你就变得足够有价值，值得被付费。

sentences.en: And it may not be from your multiple interests yet, but it can be a stepping stone that leads you into that.
sentences.zh: 这收入一开始可能不来自你的多重兴趣，但它可以成为一块垫脚石，把你引向那里。

sentences.en: That's incredible. That's why I love this path so much.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。这就是我如此热爱这条路的原因。

sentences.en: And every time I talk about this, I really have to sit and ask myself, am I just like promoting this dogma?
sentences.zh: 每次我谈到这个，我真的得坐下来问自己，我是不是在推销某种教条？

sentences.en: I tell people, start a personal brand, become a creator because it makes a lot of sense to me, and I feel like I start to touted as this one true way.
sentences.zh: 我告诉人们，去建立个人品牌，去成为一个创作者，因为这对我来说非常合理，我发现自己开始把它吹捧成唯一的正道。

sentences.en: But then, like, the more I break it down, the more it seems like the one true way.
sentences.zh: 但接着，我越是拆解它，它就越像是唯一的正道。

sentences.en: I don't know how to put it like I've heard objections to it, and those hold a lot of truth.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么说，我听过一些反对意见，那些意见确实有道理。

sentences.en: Like, well, not everyone can do this.
sentences.zh: 比如，不是每个人都能做到。

sentences.en: And my answer to that is, well, anyone can.
sentences.zh: 而我的回答是，任何人都可以。

sentences.en: The ambitious people who want to.
sentences.zh: 那些有野心、想做的人可以。

sentences.en: Everyone can't do everything right.
sentences.zh: 没有人能什么都做到，对吧。

sentences.en: It like, there's so many things in life where, it's limited to the amount of people that can do it, but this has more opportunity than most of those things, and it's all within your control.
sentences.zh: 生活中很多事情，能做到的人是有限的，但这件事比大多数事情机会都多，而且完全在你掌控之中。

sentences.en: That's what I love about it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我喜欢它的原因。

sentences.en: Now, the other thing that I love about it is that it flips the traditional model on its head so that with so with the traditional business model, you need a customer avatar and you need to niche down to that customer avatar.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它的另一点是，它把传统模式完全颠覆了——传统商业模式里，你需要一个客户画像，然后针对那个画像去细分。

sentences.en: But with this model, you are the customer avatar and that makes things so much more palatable.
sentences.zh: 但在这个模式里，你就是那个客户画像，这让一切都变得更容易接受。

sentences.en: You don't need to understand or learn that much, because if you need market research, you just look at your story, you think back on your life.
sentences.zh: 你不需要理解或学习太多东西，因为如果你需要做市场调研，你只需要看看自己的故事，回顾你的人生。

sentences.en: So you pursue your goals in life and develop yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以你去追求你的人生目标，去发展自己。

sentences.en: And by doing that, you have already validated the usefulness of what you will offer, and then you help the past version of yourself reach that same goal.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，你已经验证了你将提供的东西是有用的，然后你帮助过去的自己达到同样的目标。

sentences.en: Now, one thing you're going to have to deal with here is a lot of the business gurus like Alex were Mozi.
sentences.zh: 有一件事你必须面对，很多商业导师，比如 Alex Hormozi。

sentences.en: I love Alex for Mozi. Nothing against them.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢 Alex Hormozi，对他们没有意见。

sentences.en: They will tell you to sell to the rich so you may not have been a rich person in your past and that's okay.
sentences.zh: 他们会告诉你要卖给富人，你可能过去不是一个富人，这没关系。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that this way doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 这不意味着这条路行不通。

sentences.en: It's just an alternative route for people who have that like deep desire to do something more creative and spend a lot of their time on what they deem meaningful.
sentences.zh: 这只是另一条路，给那些有强烈渴望去做更有创造性的事、把大量时间花在自己认为有意义的事情上的人。

sentences.en: Not to say that the other way isn't meaningful.
sentences.zh: 不是说另一条路就没有意义。

sentences.en: I think you're getting the distinction here.
sentences.zh: 我想你明白这个区别了。

sentences.en: So it has to be somewhat of a conscious choice.
sentences.zh: 所以这必须是一种有意识的选择。

sentences.en: But that also doesn't mean that you're limited in any way to brag.
sentences.zh: 但这也不意味着你在任何方面受到限制。

sentences.en: I guess, like, I've made a lot of frickin money doing this.
sentences.zh: 我想说，我做这件事赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I never would have thought that I've been able to make this much money.
sentences.zh: 我从来没想过自己能赚这么多钱。

sentences.en: I'm starting a bigger well, I've been working on a software company for a long time now.
sentences.zh: 我正在启动一个更大的——其实我已经在一家软件公司上花了很长时间。

sentences.en: I'm working on a new Tropic company.
sentences.zh: 我正在做一个新的 Tropic 公司。

sentences.en: More details on that.
sentences.zh: 细节之后再说。

sentences.en: That is very cool, but I wouldn't have had these opportunities.
sentences.zh: 那非常酷，但我本来不会有这些机会。

sentences.en: It's just so cool.
sentences.zh: 这真的太酷了。

sentences.en: But with that, I'm going to give a caveat.
sentences.zh: 但说到这里，我要给一个提醒。

sentences.en: Don't be a YouTube creator.
sentences.zh: 不要做一个 YouTube 创作者。

sentences.en: Don't be a personal brand.
sentences.zh: 不要做一个个人品牌。

sentences.en: Even though I just said that don't be an influencer, be you, but in a place where your work can be discovered, followed, and supported right now and for the foreseeable future, that's on the internet.
sentences.zh: 虽然我刚说了那些，不要做一个网红，做你自己，但要在一个你的作品能被发现、被关注、被支持的地方，现在以及可预见的未来，那个地方就是互联网。

sentences.en: So if we think of Jordan Peterson, regardless of your opinion, he's not a content creator.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们想到 Jordan Peterson，不管你对他的看法如何，他不是一个内容创作者。

sentences.en: He goes on tours, he writes books.
sentences.zh: 他做巡演，他写书。

sentences.en: He even has, like Peterson Academy, which is an online very well done course.
sentences.zh: 他甚至做了 Peterson Academy，一个做得非常好的线上课程。

sentences.en: But he leverages social media as his base, and he uses the tools available to him to spread his life's work.
sentences.zh: 但他把社交媒体当作自己的根据地，用一切可用的工具去传播他毕生的事业。

sentences.en: He isn't worried about the latest content or idea trend, because his own mind transcends any of the growth strategies that you can find the quality and uniqueness in how he says his ideas is what sets him apart.
sentences.zh: 他不在乎最新的内容趋势或点子趋势，因为他自己的头脑本身就超越了任何增长策略，他表达想法的方式所带有的质量和独特性，才是他脱颖而出的原因。

sentences.en: So your business has to be a reflection of this just uniqueness of your mind.
sentences.zh: 所以你的生意必须是你头脑这种独特性的映射。

sentences.en: So how do we make that even more practical?
sentences.zh: 那我们怎么让它变得更可操作？

sentences.en: We need to actually talk about the three pillars brand, content, product.
sentences.zh: 我们需要真正聊聊三个支柱：品牌、内容、产品。

sentences.en: So idea five is that brand is an environment.
sentences.zh: 所以第五个想法是，品牌是一个环境。

sentences.en: So I want you to stop thinking as brand.
sentences.zh: 我希望你停止把品牌想成那样。

sentences.en: If you think about it this way as like your social media profile, right, your bio and your profile picture and your website and the cool little brand colors that you have, like mine, are black and white, simply because it's easy.
sentences.zh: 如果你把它想成你的社交媒体主页，对吧，你的简介、头像、网站，还有你那些很酷的品牌色，像我的是黑白的，纯粹是因为省事。

sentences.en: And that allows me to focus on the ideas.
sentences.zh: 这让我能把注意力放在想法上。

sentences.en: I want you to think about brand as an environment where people come to transform.
sentences.zh: 我希望你把品牌看作一个人们进来蜕变的环境。

sentences.en: Brand is the little world you are inviting others into.
sentences.zh: 品牌是你邀请别人进入的一个小世界。

sentences.en: Brand is an illustrated when a reader first visit your profile.
sentences.zh: 品牌是读者第一次访问你主页时被呈现出来的东西。

sentences.en: Brand is the accumulation of ideas in your readers mind.
sentences.zh: 品牌是读者关注你 3 到 6 个月后，在他们脑海中积累起来的想法总和。

sentences.en: After 3 to 6 months of following you, you illustrate your worldview, story, and philosophy for life across every single touchpoint.
sentences.zh: 你在每一个触点上，呈现你的世界观、故事和人生哲学。

sentences.en: Your banner, profile, picture, bio link in bio, landing page design, pinned content, posts, threads, newsletters, videos and the rest.
sentences.zh: 你的横幅、头像、简介、简介里的链接、着陆页设计、置顶内容、帖子、threads、newsletter、视频，所有一切。

sentences.en: So in other words, your brand is this.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你的品牌就是这个。

sentences.en: Pause the screen. If you need to.
sentences.zh: 需要的话，暂停屏幕。

sentences.en: Your brand is your story, so it would help if you spent a day or even go on a walk and just think about it and think about where you came from.
sentences.zh: 你的品牌就是你的故事，所以你花一天时间，甚至出去走一走，好好想一想，想想你从哪里来，这会很有帮助。

sentences.en: What is the lowest point you've been?
sentences.zh: 你经历过的最低谷是什么？

sentences.en: Whether the other lows that you've been, what have you overcome?
sentences.zh: 你还经历过哪些低谷，你克服了什么？

sentences.en: What is your actual story?
sentences.zh: 你真正的故事是什么？

sentences.en: What skills have you learned?
sentences.zh: 你学到了什么技能？

sentences.en: What traits have you developed?
sentences.zh: 你培养了哪些特质？

sentences.en: What are some of your weird and extreme beliefs?
sentences.zh: 你有哪些奇怪和极端的信念？

sentences.en: What do you think that other people don't?
sentences.zh: 有哪些事是你这么想、别人不这么想的？

sentences.en: What are your contrarian takes?
sentences.zh: 你的逆向观点是什么？

sentences.en: What makes you different? Now?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你与众不同？现在。

sentences.en: When you're thinking of ideas or content or products, you need to filter them through your story or through your worldview, which kind of comes naturally once you stop trying to do it.
sentences.zh: 当你在想点子、内容或产品的时候，你需要用你的故事、你的世界观去过滤它们，一旦你不再刻意去做，这其实会自然发生。

sentences.en: Because your world views your worldview, you become a translator of ideas, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你的世界观就是你的世界观，你成了一个想法的翻译者，对吧？

sentences.en: Because no idea is really original.
sentences.zh: 因为没有哪个想法是真正原创的。

sentences.en: We disguise stealing like an artist as research, right?
sentences.zh: 我们把像艺术家一样偷窃，伪装成研究，对吧？

sentences.en: Where I research ideas that I really like and I learn about them, and then I kind of translate them.
sentences.zh: 我研究我真正喜欢的想法，去学习它们，然后我某种程度上把它们翻译出来。

sentences.en: I have a topic for my newsletter, for my video, and then I look at what other people have said about that, and I think about the books that I've read, or if I'm reading a book now and then I pick and choose ideas and kind of tie them into something new and say them in my own words.
sentences.zh: 我给我的 newsletter 和视频定一个主题，然后去看别人对这个主题说过什么，回想我读过的书，或者如果正在读一本书，就从中挑选想法，把它们编织成新的东西，用我自己的话说出来。

sentences.en: And that alone is unique enough.
sentences.zh: 光这一点就已经足够独特了。

sentences.en: So when I say filter things through your story, that doesn't mean that you have to talk about yourself all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以当我说“用你的故事去过滤一切”，并不是说你要一直讲自己。

sentences.en: Of course, personal stories are personal anecdotes like I gave at the beginning of this video when I said I used to learn and learn and learn, I got stuck in tutorial hell.
sentences.zh: 当然，个人故事就是个人轶事，比如我在视频开头讲的——我以前学啊学啊学，陷进了教程地狱。

sentences.en: That's a relatable aspect of this, but that's not necessarily what I mean.
sentences.zh: 那是让人有共鸣的部分，但这不完全是我想表达的意思。

sentences.en: I mean translating now the difficult part for a lot of people, and this was myself included, is that you don't really think your story is worth telling because you think it's boring or you haven't reflected on your growth, but it is, and you'll come to realize that.
sentences.zh: 我指的是转化。对很多人来说，困难的地方在于——我自己以前也是这样——你不觉得自己的故事值得讲，因为你认为它很无聊，或者你没有反思过自己的成长。但它值得，你最终会意识到的。

sentences.en: So now the point with everything that I'm saying is that your bio in your profile picture and your website colors, they do not matter at all.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在说的这一切，核心在于：你的个人简介、头像、网站配色，这些根本不重要。

sentences.en: If you go on any social media, you're going to see people with profile pictures that are just like weird scribbles or a singular color like blue or red.
sentences.zh: 你随便打开一个社交媒体，都会看到有人用那种奇怪的涂鸦当头像，或者就是纯色，比如蓝色或红色。

sentences.en: You're going to go to Paul Graham's website and you're going to see that he just has an HTML website, and the formatting doesn't look good at all.
sentences.zh: 你去 Paul Graham 的网站，会看到他只有一个 HTML 网站，排版一点都不好看。

sentences.en: His essays that everyone loves are literally just like the most basic aerial text you'll find ever.
sentences.zh: 他那些所有人都喜欢的文章，真的就是你见过的最基础的 Arial 字体文本。

sentences.en: It does not matter.
sentences.zh: 这不重要。

sentences.en: The quality of ideas and unique perspective is what matters.
sentences.zh: 重要的是想法的质量和独特的视角。

sentences.en: So my recommendation for branding, or at least to start thinking about your brand, is to make a list of 5 to 10 people you respect online.
sentences.zh: 所以我对品牌建设的建议——或者至少是开始思考你的品牌——是列出 5 到 10 个你在网上尊重的人。

sentences.en: These are the people that are kind of aspirational, the people you want to become like.
sentences.zh: 这些人是你的榜样，是你想成为的那种人。

sentences.en: Then you look at their profile picture, their bio and content.
sentences.zh: 然后去看他们的头像、个人简介和内容。

sentences.en: Then you take mental notes of patterns between them, and then you start formulating what you should do for your own brand with your own little spin.
sentences.zh: 然后用心记下他们之间的共同模式，再开始构思你应该怎么带着自己的风格去做自己的品牌。

sentences.en: Now, in all honesty, I wouldn't overcomplicate this or I wouldn't even really think about it until now.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我不会把这件事搞得太复杂，甚至到现在我都不太会去想它。

sentences.en: It's just going to come naturally.
sentences.zh: 它会自然形成的。

sentences.en: Don't even worry about your brand, because a lot of people get stuck on that.
sentences.zh: 根本不用去担心你的品牌，因为很多人就卡在这上面。

sentences.en: When I teach this and I used to teach it in workshops and other things, people just would put off doing anything else until they got their brand right, when it really does not matter.
sentences.zh: 我以前教这个的时候，在 workshop 和其他场合教，人们会一直拖着不做其他任何事，直到他们把品牌搞对，而实际上这根本不重要。

sentences.en: Because that's not what a brand is.
sentences.zh: 因为品牌不是那个东西。

sentences.en: A brand is what you associate yourself with the ideas you post over time, the people you talk to, the podcasts you go on.
sentences.zh: 品牌是你通过长期发布的想法、你交流的人、你上的播客，让人们把你和这些东西关联起来。

sentences.en: It's like this accumulation is just how people view you.
sentences.zh: 它就是一种积累，就是别人怎么看你。

sentences.en: And if you break down how people come to view you, then you understand it.
sentences.zh: 如果你拆解一下别人是怎么形成对你的看法的，你就明白了。

sentences.en: Now, before we get into content, I have written an article on this.
sentences.zh: 在我们进入内容部分之前，我写过一篇关于这个的文章。

sentences.en: I'll link it in the description.
sentences.zh: 我会把链接放在简介里。

sentences.en: It's called How to Build a World.
sentences.zh: 文章叫《如何构建一个世界》。

sentences.en: The two hour content ecosystem expanded, so that'll help you understand how brand is a world created through this content ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 是两小时内容生态系统的扩展版，它会帮你理解品牌是如何通过这个内容生态系统创造出来的一个世界。

sentences.en: We're not going to actual talk about how to write a newsletter and break that down into smaller pieces of content like I do in that, but that leads into number six, which is content is novel perspectives.
sentences.zh: 我们不会真的去讲怎么写 newsletter 并把它拆成更小的内容块，就像我在那篇文章里做的那样，但这引出了第六点：内容就是新颖的视角。

sentences.en: Now, I've said this for a while now, but it's more prevalent than it.
sentences.zh: 我这么说已经有一段时间了，但现在比以往任何时候都更明显。

sentences.en: It will be ever, because the internet is just continuing to become more and more of a firehose of information and AI isn't helping with that, right?
sentences.zh: 以后也会越来越明显，因为互联网正在持续变成越来越猛的信息洪流，而 AI 在这件事上没帮什么忙，对吧？

sentences.en: Anyone can generate anything.
sentences.zh: 任何人都能生成任何东西。

sentences.en: But what that means is that trust and signal are more important than ever.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着，信任和信号比以往任何时候都更重要。

sentences.en: If you hear me say signal, that means like the opposite of noise, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你听到我说“信号”，意思就是噪音的反面，对吧？

sentences.en: Noisy.
sentences.zh: 全是噪音。

sentences.en: A lot of content signals like, ooh, exciting, important need to pay attention to that.
sentences.zh: 很多内容释放的信号就像在喊：哦，这个刺激，这个重要，你得注意一下。

sentences.en: So in my opinion, the guiding light for your content should be to curate the best possible ideas in one place.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，你内容的指路明灯，应该是把最好的想法都汇聚到一个地方。

sentences.en: Your brand is a collection of all the ideas you care about in your own words, under one account on the internet.
sentences.zh: 你的品牌，就是你在互联网上一个账号下，用你自己的话，把你关心的所有想法收集起来。

sentences.en: Now, if you have any plans to do podcasts or public speaking, when you look at the best podcasters or public speakers, you see that they.
sentences.zh: 如果你有做播客或公开演讲的计划，你去看看那些最顶尖的播客主或演说家，就会发现他们。

sentences.en: If you watch multiple of their podcasts, you see that they're kind of just repeating the same 5 to 10 ideas, and they're just exposing their best ideas to new audiences.
sentences.zh: 如果你多看几期他们的节目，就会发现他们其实就是在重复那五到十个核心想法，只是把最好的想法曝光给新的受众。

sentences.en: That's all they're really doing.
sentences.zh: 他们真正在做的就只是这个。

sentences.en: They've refined their ideas enough to know that these are the ones that are the most impactful.
sentences.zh: 他们已经把想法打磨得足够透彻，知道哪些才是最有冲击力的。

sentences.en: So what you have to do is you have to experiment and try until you have those 5 to 10 ideas, and then you have to turn those 5 to 10 ideas into each, a thousand ideas, which we'll talk about now.
sentences.zh: 所以你要做的就是不断实验、不断尝试，直到你找到那五到十个想法，然后你得把这五到十个想法，每一个都演化出一千个想法，这个我们马上会讲。

sentences.en: I really think a metric to aim for in your content is idea density, which means that the amount of high signal or really good ideas is just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为，你内容应该追求的一个指标是想法密度，也就是说，高信号或者说真正好的想法无处不在。

sentences.en: And that slowly increases over time, with time and effort.
sentences.zh: 随着时间和精力的投入，这个密度会慢慢提升。

sentences.en: And that's what creates a brand that's worth following and paying for, because you just hit the mark all the time.
sentences.zh: 这就是打造一个值得关注、值得付费的品牌的原因，因为你总能命中要害。

sentences.en: So the goal of curating ideas to include under your brand should fall at the intersection of one performance, which is ideas that have the potential to do well.
sentences.zh: 所以，为你的品牌筛选想法的目标，应该落在两个东西的交汇点上：一是表现力，也就是那些有潜力跑出来的想法。

sentences.en: And this is a measure of how much other people will care, and to excitement, which is the ideas that give you a sense of excitement to write about them.
sentences.zh: 这衡量的是别人会在多大程度上关心它；二是兴奋感，也就是那些让你写起来就感到兴奋的想法。

sentences.en: This is a measure of how much you care, so it's a balance when choosing what ideas to post.
sentences.zh: 这衡量的是你有多在乎，所以在选择发什么想法时，这是一个平衡。

sentences.en: It's a balance of art and business.
sentences.zh: 这是艺术和商业的平衡。

sentences.en: Are other people going to care about this?
sentences.zh: 别人会关心这个吗？

sentences.en: Has this done well before or do I have a good hook?
sentences.zh: 这个以前跑得好吗？或者我有没有一个好的钩子？

sentences.en: Do I have other things and what you care about?
sentences.zh: 我有没有别的东西，以及你自己在乎什么？

sentences.en: So it's not blatantly copying what works, it's doing something unique, but also taking into account the principles that are actually going to capture attention.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是明目张胆地抄袭有效的东西，而是做独特的内容，但同时也要考虑到那些真正能抓住注意力的原则。

sentences.en: So how do we do this?
sentences.zh: 那我们具体怎么做？

sentences.en: Step one is to build an idea museum.
sentences.zh: 第一步，建一个想法博物馆。

sentences.en: This can this is the most useful thing.
sentences.zh: 这可以——这是最有用的东西。

sentences.en: In other words, this just means build.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这就是让你去建。

sentences.en: A swipe file is what marketers call it.
sentences.zh: 营销人管它叫素材库。

sentences.en: So it lists can be a document.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一个文档。

sentences.en: It can be a folder in Eden or Notion or Google Docs.
sentences.zh: 可以是 Eden、Notion 或 Google Docs 里的一个文件夹。

sentences.en: If you don't have access to Eden yet, join the waitlist.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没用上 Eden，去加入候补名单。

sentences.en: We're releasing the next cohort round soon.
sentences.zh: 我们很快会开放下一批内测。

sentences.en: If you don't know what it is, it's an intelligent drive.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不知道它是什么，它是一个智能硬盘。

sentences.en: You can store all of your files, PDFs, videos, etc. you can search all of those things by frame.
sentences.zh: 你可以存储所有文件、PDF、视频等等，还能按帧搜索所有这些内容。

sentences.en: You can paste YouTube links, social media links.
sentences.zh: 你可以粘贴 YouTube 链接、社交媒体链接。

sentences.en: It transcribes, downloads the video, makes it all reference a bowl with AI, so you can put it inside a canvas or project, and it brings this unique way of working.
sentences.zh: 它会转录、下载视频，用 AI 让所有内容都可引用，这样你就能把它放进画布或项目里，带来一种独特的工作方式。

sentences.en: It's a workspace for your creative work, and it allows you to replace things like Google Drive or, certain AI apps like Cloud or ChatGPT, and even things like frame for video editors if you need to share videos, comment on them.
sentences.zh: 它是你创造性工作的工作空间，让你能替代 Google Drive、某些 AI 应用比如 Claude 或 ChatGPT，甚至替代像 Frame 这样的视频审阅工具，如果你需要分享视频、在上面留言的话。

sentences.en: So on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: But the point is that you need somewhere to jot down ideas as soon as they come to mind.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，你需要一个地方，在想法冒出来的时候立刻记下来。

sentences.en: This is a critical habit.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关键习惯。

sentences.en: So when other people teach you how to create content, and I've done this in the past, I'll actually link to another thing called the content map, which helps you figure all of this out and creates like a web of content ideas that you can write about, but people have you focus on like 2 or 3 content pillars, maybe even one, and then you break those down into topics and sub topics
sentences.zh: 别人教你做内容的时候——我以前也这么教过——我会推荐一个叫内容地图的东西，帮你理清这一切，形成一个内容创意的网络，让你有东西可写。但他们让你聚焦在两三个内容支柱上，甚至一个，然后拆分成话题和子话题，

sentences.en: and other things of that nature. That's very useful.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。这确实很有用。

sentences.en: But if you want to avoid all of that, just focus on the ideas that are important to you and share those. That's it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想跳过所有这些，就只关注那些对你来说重要的想法，然后分享出去。就这样。

sentences.en: That's your entire content strategy.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的全部内容策略。

sentences.en: Now, step two is to curate based on idea density.
sentences.zh: 好，第二步是根据想法密度来筛选。

sentences.en: So how do you actually start filling this idea Museum?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么真正开始填充这个"想法博物馆"？

sentences.en: Do you just scroll around?
sentences.zh: 就到处刷吗？

sentences.en: You just think of ideas. What do you do?
sentences.zh: 就凭空想吗？你到底该怎么做？

sentences.en: The best way, in my opinion, is to have 3 to 5 sources of information that have high idea density.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，最好的方式是拥有3到5个高想法密度的信息来源。

sentences.en: So what that means is just have 3 to 5 sources of information where when you go to them, you consistently think, damn, I wish I wrote that and you have to do this without judgment, because something that you think has been said over and over again, to the point where it doesn't matter anymore, or something you think is too basic, or that everyone knows this.
sentences.zh: 意思是，有3到5个信息来源，当你接触它们时，你会反复冒出这个念头：靠，真希望这是我写的。而且你必须不带评判地去做这件事，因为有些东西你觉得已经被说烂了，说到毫无意义了，或者你觉得太基础了，觉得所有人都知道。

sentences.en: Avoid letting any of those cloud your mind.
sentences.zh: 别让这些念头蒙蔽你。

sentences.en: Just jot down the idea and then you're going to reframe it.
sentences.zh: 把想法记下来，然后你会重新表述它。

sentences.en: Post it.
sentences.zh: 发出去。

sentences.en: So the most idea dense sources of information in my opinion, isn't just scrolling social media.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，想法密度最高的信息来源，不是刷社交媒体。

sentences.en: It's things like old or little known books.
sentences.zh: 而是那些古老或鲜为人知的书。

sentences.en: So as an example, I have five books that I reread over and over again because the ideas are just so good.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我有五本书，反复读了一遍又一遍，因为里面的想法实在是太好了。

sentences.en: These are where the timeless principles live.
sentences.zh: 那些永恒的原则就住在这些书里。

sentences.en: They're untouched by trends.
sentences.zh: 它们不被潮流触碰。

sentences.en: The second place is curated blogs, accounts or books.
sentences.zh: 第二个地方是精选过的博客、账号或书籍。

sentences.en: So these are like accounts that are doing the same thing as you kind of sort of. Not really.
sentences.zh: 这些账号跟你做的事有点类似，但不完全是。

sentences.en: But these are blogs like Farnam Street, which curate the best ideas for modern intellectuals, accounts like Nouvel ism, which curate novels, best ideas, or books like the Maxwell Daily Reader, which has Maxwell's best ideas one day at a time for a year.
sentences.zh: 比如像 Farnam Street 这样的博客，为现代知识分子精选最好的想法；像 Nouvel ism 这样的账号，精选小说里最好的想法；或者像《Maxwell Daily Reader》这样的书，把 Maxwell 最好的想法按一天一篇排满一整年。

sentences.en: And sources like these do a lot of the heavy lifting for you, because you're just being exposed to, like, all of these incredible, validated ideas.
sentences.zh: 这类来源帮你做了大量的重活，因为你直接接触到的都是这些经过验证的、令人惊叹的想法。

sentences.en: Of course, you should discover some on your own, like when you're watching a YouTube video and you spot something in the middle of a video and be like, oh, that's good, or while you're scrolling social media.
sentences.zh: 当然，你也应该自己去发现一些，比如看 YouTube 视频时，在中间捕捉到某个东西，心想"哦，这个好"，或者刷社交媒体的时候。

sentences.en: But if you struggle to come up with ideas, go that route.
sentences.zh: 但如果你苦于想不出点子，就走那条路。

sentences.en: Now, the third place is just heavy hitting social accounts.
sentences.zh: 第三个地方是那些重磅的社交账号。

sentences.en: So I personally have a list of maybe five social accounts that always post great ideas.
sentences.zh: 我个人有一个列表，大概五个社交账号，它们总是发布很棒的想法。

sentences.en: If I don't have something to write about, I'll scroll through their page for inspiration and find something that I have an opinion on, and then I'll write about that.
sentences.zh: 如果我没什么可写的，我就去翻他们的页面找灵感，找到一个我有自己观点的东西，然后写那个。

sentences.en: Now, step three is to learn how to write one idea 1000 different ways, because that's all this game is, is you have your 5 to 10, maybe 20 best ideas, and then you just rewrite those over and over again from all different angles.
sentences.zh: 好，第三步是学会用一千种不同的方式写同一个想法，因为这个游戏的全部就是：你有5到10个，也许20个最好的想法，然后你从各种不同的角度，一遍又一遍地重写它们。

sentences.en: And that's even more effective now than it was before, because I can generate all information. Right?
sentences.zh: 这在现在比以前更有效，因为我能生成所有信息。对吧？

sentences.en: People are following you because you don't have all information.
sentences.zh: 人们关注你，恰恰是因为你没有所有信息。

sentences.en: You have a very niche, even though it's not really niche.
sentences.zh: 你有一个非常细分的领域，尽管它其实不算细分。

sentences.en: When you're talking about a bunch of different things, it's niche and spirit compared to a lot, because becoming a good writer or speaker isn't only about the idea, but how you articulate the idea.
sentences.zh: 当你谈论一堆不同的事情时，它在精神上其实是非常垂直的，因为成为一个好的写作者或演讲者，不只是关于想法本身，更在于你如何表达这个想法。

sentences.en: The idea does a lot of the heavy lifting, but the structure of the idea, how it's articulated, does even more so.
sentences.zh: 想法本身承担了很大一部分工作，但想法的结构、它被表达的方式，承担得更多。

sentences.en: To show you what I mean, just take this post structure.
sentences.zh: 为了让你明白我的意思，直接看这个帖子结构。

sentences.en: This is a post I wrote before.
sentences.zh: 这是我之前写的一个帖子。

sentences.en: One pattern I've noticed and happy people.
sentences.zh: 我在快乐的人身上注意到一个模式。

sentences.en: They're obsessed about maintaining their mental clarity.
sentences.zh: 他们痴迷于维护自己的思维清晰度。

sentences.en: So the idea here is that happy people maintain their mental clarity.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的想法是：快乐的人会维护自己的思维清晰度。

sentences.en: The structure is formatted in two parts a hook in the form of an observation and the delivery of what the observation is.
sentences.zh: 结构分成两部分：一个观察形式的钩子，以及对这个观察的展开。

sentences.en: So it seems simple, but one idea with two different structures can drastically change how the idea does so.
sentences.zh: 看起来很简单，但同一个想法用两种不同的结构，会彻底改变这个想法的效果。

sentences.en: Ideas are cheap, but articulation of the ideas is expensive and you need to learn how to articulate them well.
sentences.zh: 想法很廉价，但对想法的表达很昂贵，你需要学会如何把它们表达好。

sentences.en: As an example of another structure, let's take the same idea.
sentences.zh: 作为另一个结构的例子，我们用同一个想法。

sentences.en: Happy people are obsessed of maintaining their mental clarity.
sentences.zh: 快乐的人痴迷于维护自己的思维清晰度。

sentences.en: So it would look like this.
sentences.zh: 那么它会变成这样。

sentences.en: Happy people are clear minded people.
sentences.zh: 快乐的人是头脑清晰的人。

sentences.en: They take time for rest.
sentences.zh: 他们会花时间休息。

sentences.en: They focus on one singular goal.
sentences.zh: 他们专注于一个单一目标。

sentences.en: They ruthlessly eliminate distractions.
sentences.zh: 他们无情地消除干扰。

sentences.en: In other words, happy people are obsessive about maintaining their mental clarity.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，快乐的人痴迷于维护自己的思维清晰度。

sentences.en: It's the same idea, a different structure and a different impact.
sentences.zh: 同一个想法，不同的结构，不同的冲击力。

sentences.en: The first one is probably going to do a bit better.
sentences.zh: 第一个可能效果会更好一些。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean the second one is bad, it just shows that this is a skill.
sentences.zh: 这不代表第二个就不好，它只是说明这是一项技能。

sentences.en: So what I recommend is every idea you come across for now, as you're practicing, write it in a few different ways and post them in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以我建议，从现在开始，你遇到的每一个想法，在练习阶段，都用几种不同的方式写出来，然后就这样发出去。

sentences.en: Those two posts that I showed you practically the same thing, but they're distinctly different posts.
sentences.zh: 我给你看的那两个帖子，本质上是一回事，但它们是截然不同的两个帖子。

sentences.en: So when you come across an idea, you add it to your idea museum or just take it down in your notes and then you turn it into a different structure.
sentences.zh: 所以当你遇到一个想法，把它加到你的想法博物馆里，或者就记在你的笔记里，然后把它转化成不同的结构。

sentences.en: But how do you actually do that?
sentences.zh: 但具体怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Okay, you go to your idea museum and you look at all of the ideas in there, and then you break down the structures of those things and you start to create a second idea, museum of structures that you can use.
sentences.zh: 好，你去你的想法博物馆，看里面所有的想法，然后拆解这些东西的结构，开始创建第二个博物馆——一个你可以使用的结构博物馆。

sentences.en: So you practice this by the first three ideas that you mark down.
sentences.zh: 所以你练习的方式是：拿你记下来的前三个想法。

sentences.en: You break down the structure of how those things work, and then you kind of interchange them right, like a three by three matrix.
sentences.zh: 拆解这些东西的结构是怎么运作的，然后你开始把它们互换，就像一个三乘三的矩阵。

sentences.en: So you take idea one, plug it into idea three structure and you practice writing like that.
sentences.zh: 你拿想法一，塞进想法三的结构里，然后就这样练习写作。

sentences.en: Now what I recommend here is just employing AI for help.
sentences.zh: 这里我建议直接用 AI 来帮忙。

sentences.en: AI is very good at helping you learn how to do this.
sentences.zh: AI 非常擅长帮你学习怎么做这件事。

sentences.en: It's not very good at writing for you.
sentences.zh: 它不太擅长替你写。

sentences.en: And again, we'll talk about that in the next video.
sentences.zh: 这个我们下个视频再聊。

sentences.en: But you can use this prompt which is do a comprehensive analysis on this social post, the overall idea how the sentences are structured and choice of words.
sentences.zh: 但你可以用这个提示词：对这个社交媒体帖子做一个全面分析，包括整体想法、句子是如何结构的、以及用词选择。

sentences.en: Analyze why people engage with it, why it works so well, what psychological tactics are being used, and how I can replicate this style step by step with my own ideas.
sentences.zh: 分析人们为什么会互动，为什么效果这么好，用了哪些心理策略，以及我如何一步步用自己的想法复现这种风格。

sentences.en: So you paste the prompt, you use something like Claude, and then you can either paste one post or maybe one newsletter or multiple posts into it, and it's going to create like a little mini course on why those worked and how to replicate it.
sentences.zh: 你粘贴提示词，用 Claude 之类的工具，然后你可以把一篇帖子、一期 newsletter 或者多篇帖子扔进去，它会生成一个迷你课程，告诉你这些内容为什么有效、怎么复现。

sentences.en: And then you take another idea and then you practice.
sentences.zh: 然后你拿另一个想法去练习。

sentences.en: And seriously, those are all of my secrets for content.
sentences.zh: 说真的，这就是我做内容的全部秘诀。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜你。

sentences.en: You just went through an entire course on content creation.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚上完了一整套内容创作课。

sentences.en: That's all you need.
sentences.zh: 你需要的就这些。

sentences.en: But of course, there's also the skill of how to grow without relying on the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 但当然，还有一个技能：如何不依赖算法实现增长。

sentences.en: So watch the last video if you haven't already, which is how to build an audience starting from zero followers.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你还没看上一期视频，去看一下，讲的是如何从零粉丝开始建立受众。

sentences.en: This just the last video.
sentences.zh: 就是上一期视频。

sentences.en: Now this video is getting long, so we're going to speed things up a bit.
sentences.zh: 这期视频已经很长了，我们加快一点节奏。

sentences.en: But idea number seven is that systems are the new product.
sentences.zh: 第七个想法是：系统就是新的产品。

sentences.en: And I'm also speeding this up because I'm linking an entire guide to how I create profitable products.
sentences.zh: 我加快讲这部分，也是因为我会附上一个完整指南，讲我如何打造盈利产品。

sentences.en: And that goes over it much more in depth than I want to do here.
sentences.zh: 那个指南比我在这里展开讲要深入得多。

sentences.en: But at this point in time, we are in a systems economy.
sentences.zh: 但此时此刻，我们身处一个系统经济时代。

sentences.en: People don't want a solution to their problems.
sentences.zh: 人们要的不是一个能解决他们问题的方案。

sentences.en: They want your solution to their problems.
sentences.zh: 他们要的是你的方案，来解决他们的问题。

sentences.en: There are tons of writing products out there.
sentences.zh: 市面上有无数写作类产品。

sentences.en: So what makes my product to our writer stand out?
sentences.zh: 那我的产品 To Our Writer 凭什么脱颖而出？

sentences.en: Or even Eden?
sentences.zh: 或者 Eden 呢？

sentences.en: What makes the software that's going to compete with Google Drive?
sentences.zh: 一个要和 Google Drive 竞争的软件，凭什么？

sentences.en: That there was a comment in the YouTube video on Matt and Ari, the co-founders channel, saying that we have no competitive edge, but I don't think they use Eden and they definitely don't understand where we're going.
sentences.zh: YouTube 上 Matt 和 Ari 联合创始人频道的视频下面有条评论，说我们没有竞争优势，但我觉得他们没用过 Eden，而且他们绝对不理解我们要去往哪里。

sentences.en: Nobody understands that that's in our head and we could easily get replaced or made irrelevant by Google.
sentences.zh: 没人理解那些东西在我们脑子里，我们随时可能被 Google 取代或者变得无关紧要。

sentences.en: But the difference is that these are hyper specific systems that I made for myself.
sentences.zh: 但区别在于，这些是我为自己打造的高度定制化系统。

sentences.en: The deeper layer to that is that these are hyper specific systems that I made for people with the same problems as me, and no big conglomerate corporation is going to pay attention to as much detail and effectiveness as I'm going to, or my team is going to for the specific type of person that can benefit from a more specific system.
sentences.zh: 更深一层的是，这些是我为和我有同样问题的人打造的高度定制化系统，没有哪个大型企业集团会像我、或者我的团队那样，为一个能从更精准系统中获益的特定人群，去关注那么多细节和有效性。

sentences.en: With Eden, we're kind of toeing the line there, right?
sentences.zh: 在 Eden 上，我们确实有点踩线，对吧？

sentences.en: It is more general.
sentences.zh: 它更通用一些。

sentences.en: We're trying to encapsulate more, but at the end of the day, it's for creatives.
sentences.zh: 我们想囊括更多，但归根结底，它是为创意工作者打造的。

sentences.en: It's for creators who have ideas, want to synthesize them, want to resurface them when they need to.
sentences.zh: 它是为那些有想法、想整合想法、想在需要时重新调出想法的创作者打造的。

sentences.en: You need to connect them.
sentences.zh: 你需要把它们连接起来。

sentences.en: You need to work with them in a project and not have ten browser tabs open for all of your different research and your books in your AI apps and everything like that.
sentences.zh: 你需要在一个项目里处理它们，而不是为了各种研究、书籍、AI 应用开十个浏览器标签页。

sentences.en: I mean, Google can't do that because docs, slides, sheets, all of that is isolated by necessity.
sentences.zh: 我是说，Google 做不到这一点，因为 Docs、Slides、Sheets 这些东西本质上就是彼此隔离的。

sentences.en: It's in different tabs and Google Drive, frankly, just has a terrible UX.
sentences.zh: 它们在不同的标签页里，而且说实话，Google Drive 的用户体验真的很差。

sentences.en: So for to our writer specifically, this all starts with identifying and solving problems in your life in a unique way.
sentences.zh: 所以具体到 To Our Writer，这一切都始于：识别你生活中的问题，然后用一种独特的方式去解决它们。

sentences.en: So I had trouble having an endless source of content ideas.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时的问题是，没有一个源源不断的内容创意来源。

sentences.en: I just struggled to come up with content ideas.
sentences.zh: 我就是很难想出内容点子。

sentences.en: And two, I didn't want to waste a ton of time creating content for all different platforms.
sentences.zh: 其次，我不想浪费大量时间，为每个不同的平台单独创作内容。

sentences.en: So that's why I started experimenting with different systems.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我开始尝试不同的系统。

sentences.en: And my goal was pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 我的目标非常明确。

sentences.en: I wanted to write all of my content in two hours a day.
sentences.zh: 我想把所有的内容写作压缩在每天两小时内完成。

sentences.en: So I had a constraint and that bred creativity.
sentences.zh: 我给自己设了一个限制，这个限制反而催生了创造力。

sentences.en: So I started testing solutions for more content ideas.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始测试各种方案，来解决内容创意不足的问题。

sentences.en: I created swipe files, steps to generate ideas that worked for me, and templates to use if I still couldn't think of anything.
sentences.zh: 我创建了素材库、对我有效的创意生成步骤，还有实在想不出东西时可以用的模板。

sentences.en: And then I looked over my week.
sentences.zh: 然后我审视了自己的一周。

sentences.en: This is a very useful practice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有用的做法。

sentences.en: If you're going to create a product is how does an individual's week look right?
sentences.zh: 如果你打算做一个产品，就要问：一个人的一周到底长什么样？

sentences.en: What did I want to do?
sentences.zh: 我想做什么？

sentences.en: How was I going to create content?
sentences.zh: 我打算怎么创作内容？

sentences.en: One newsletter a week seems reasonable.
sentences.zh: 每周一封 newsletter，看起来合理。

sentences.en: The three posts a day, at least on something like Twitter, seemed reasonable.
sentences.zh: 每天发三条帖子，至少在 Twitter 这样的平台上，看起来合理。

sentences.en: One thread a week seemed reasonable.
sentences.zh: 每周一条长帖，看起来合理。

sentences.en: Okay, do all of these things have to be unique content?
sentences.zh: 好，那这些东西都必须是独一无二的内容吗？

sentences.en: Do can I talk about one theme per week?
sentences.zh: 我能不能每周只讲一个主题？

sentences.en: Can I write the newsletter and then pull social media posts from that?
sentences.zh: 我能不能先写 newsletter，然后从中拆出社交媒体帖子？

sentences.en: So on, so forth. And so I started testing that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。然后我就开始测试这个思路。

sentences.en: And when you start testing something that you created on like a week long timescale, then you start to encounter problems and then you fix those problems to improve the system and then things start to flow.
sentences.zh: 当你开始以一周为周期，去测试你自己创造的东西时，你就会遇到问题，然后你解决这些问题，改进系统，事情就开始顺畅运转了。

sentences.en: So doing this, I realized that I could cross post to just every platform, right?
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，我意识到我可以直接同步发布到每一个平台。

sentences.en: Most people won't even try that because they think that people will get mad that they're repeating themselves.
sentences.zh: 大多数人连试都不会试，因为他们觉得别人会反感自己重复发同样的内容。

sentences.en: But frankly, I haven't noticed anything.
sentences.zh: 但坦白说，我什么都没注意到。

sentences.en: Maybe like one person is like, why are you repeating the same content on all platforms?
sentences.zh: 可能只有一个人说过，你为什么在所有平台发一样的内容？

sentences.en: But they still do well because people are usually just consuming it on one platform.
sentences.zh: 但这些内容表现依然很好，因为人们通常只在一个平台上消费内容。

sentences.en: So why would I waste my time to spread my ideas thin and try to create something new for each platform that would result in a decrease in quality, rather than focus on less content with higher quality ideas and do those once a week.
sentences.zh: 那我为什么要浪费时间，把我的想法摊薄，试图为每个平台创作新内容，导致质量下降，而不是专注于更少的内容、更高质量的想法，每周只做一次？

sentences.en: And my hypothesis was correct.
sentences.zh: 我的假设是对的。

sentences.en: That's literally the foundation of everything that I've done.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我后来所做一切的基础。

sentences.en: And then from there I realized, okay, my newsletter can go on to my blog just so people can access it if they weren't on the email list.
sentences.zh: 从那时起我意识到，好，我的 newsletter 可以放到我的博客上，这样不在邮件列表里的人也能看到。

sentences.en: And then it can turn into a YouTube outline, and it's like the YouTube video can also go into the podcast.
sentences.zh: 然后它可以变成 YouTube 视频大纲，YouTube 视频又可以变成播客。

sentences.en: I literally have all platforms on one piece of content a week that's broken down into the rest.
sentences.zh: 我所有的平台，真的就是靠每周一个核心内容，然后拆解成其他形式。

sentences.en: So in a nutshell, and without going too deep into it, that's how you stand out in a world of products.
sentences.zh: 所以简单来说，不往太深里讲，这就是你如何在一个充满产品的世界里脱颖而出的方法。

sentences.en: So thank you for watching this far.
sentences.zh: 感谢你看到这里。

sentences.en: I deeply appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: As I said, all of the links mentioned are in the description.
sentences.zh: 我说过的所有链接都在简介里。

sentences.en: Subscribe for the next video on the future of work and watch the last video.
sentences.zh: 订阅我，下期聊工作的未来，也别忘了看上期视频。

sentences.en: If you'd like to learn how to actually build an audience without relying on the algorithm, like subscribe before you leave.
sentences.zh: 如果你想学会不靠算法真正建立起自己的受众，走之前点个赞、订阅一下。

sentences.en: Again, thank you for watching. Bye.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢观看。再见。
